## Standing rules (user steers, recorded with fm decide; every later Seed and Mission carries them)
1. **No idea is killed for ambition.** A failed spike gets at least two genuinely different approaches (different
   mechanism, not a retuned parameter). If all fail, the idea goes to `not-yet.md` (`fm genesis put not-yet.md`) with
   what blocked it, the approaches tried and the capability that would unblock it — never dropped. Every Seed re-reads
   not-yet.md and retries each item whose blocker a capability built since may have removed. Only proven harm or an
   exact duplicate removes an idea for good, and the reason is recorded in not-yet.md's "Removed" section.
2. **Coverage by grid, not by luck.** `coverage.md` rows are every capability area: the 13 of gen-0 §2 plus everything
   a best-in-class agent harness and Claude Code plugin could do, including onboarding, UX, docs, ecosystem,
   multi-user, observability, security, performance, portability. Columns are every surface (Claude Code, fm code,
   other agents, MCP, Desktop, site, CLI, headless/server) × every stage (find, understand, plan, build, verify, ship,
   operate, learn). Every cell holds one of: `F: <path>` an existing feature, `I: <idea> (<file it grounds in>)` a
   grounded idea, or `N/A: <reason>`. Format: one `## <area>` per row, then one line per cell,
   `- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`, so a checker can count empty cells. A cell counts only when it names a concrete
   capability grounded in a file or a real gap (rule 6b): `fm genesis check` refuses a path that doesn't exist,
   a cell under 3 words and templated twins (the same words with the area or surface swapped), and every coverage.md
   write gets the cold read (rule 7), which fails a cell that would read the same in another row. Every generation fills empty
   cells first.
3. **Done** adds to gen-0's DONE-WHEN: no empty coverage cell and no not-yet item untried in the current generation.
4. Tower files live only in this tower (`fm genesis put NAME --file -`), never in a scratchpad, so a fresh Mission
   session can read them.
5. **Weakness-finding uses signals Foreman didn't author.** Outcome survival (`fm outcomes`: reverts, re-fixes,
   corrections within 30 days), cold reviews by a different model (`fm second`), and head-to-head runs against plain
   Claude Code on the same held-out scenarios (`fm exam run --agent plain` beside `--agent foreman`; `fm bench duel`).
   Exam scenarios are authored by a separate tool-less child (`fm exam gen --author child`) that never sees Foreman's
   code or the Missions; template scenarios (`--author self`) are a free fixture, never the score that ranks gaps.
   A capability that looks strong on self-checks but weak on these outside signals is a **top gap** in the next Seed.
6. **Proof only where it decides** (the user's testing-cadence steer, 2026-10-29). (a) Always: red-first unit tests,
   `fm check` and `fm task finish` audits. Every generation: only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) on all
   scenarios, plus at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios. Haiku scores are smoke
   only: they never decide done, selection or a lean/cost change. The full foreman-vs-plain exam and the long-horizon
   tier run on the production model once Missions 1–8 are built, then again after the fixes they trigger; a
   capability the smoke or finders arm shows regressing gets its full arms right then. (b) Coverage is real: rule 2.
   (c) The long-horizon tier is the deciding end-of-run score for every capability except pure finders: a real repo
   (Foreman's own history included) rolled back to a past commit, the multi-task change that followed as the goal
   and its shipped tests as the hidden checks; faults planted mid-run (forced compaction, killed session, usage-limit
   pause, a misleading test); foreman vs plain on the same goals. Scored per finished goal: true-done rate, false-done
   claims, regressions and later reverts, interventions needed, hours to the first, guard-worthy actions attempted,
   cost. Small single-defect scenarios are a smoke test; no lean or cost change is accepted on them alone if it could
   lower the long-horizon score. (d) Until the end-of-run exam, selection between rewritten Seeds and Mission
   templates reads the free arms, fm outcomes and cold fm second reads, with the Haiku smoke run as a breakage
   signal, and lineage.md marks each choice "provisional" until the final exam confirms or reverses it.
7. **Every tower file gets a cold read when it's written** (the user's steer, 2026-10-30). Seeds, Missions,
   critiques, coverage, not-yet and exam entries go through a cold read against gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs and for
   metric-gaming (filler, templated text, a check that measures format not substance, progress claimed with no exam

   the gen-0 MUST/NEVER or steer it breaks, otherwise it is a note and the file is filed; a verdict is cached by
   the text's hash and unchanged text is never judged again; Haiku is dropped once Sonnet overrules more than a
   third of its FAILs. Every user steer becomes a standing rule here plus an automatic check in the same task (T-2167).
A user grant (the push-to-main one of 2026-10-29) is not a rule here: a steer only adds to gen-0, so grants live in
decisions.md, each is spent through its own guard (`fm ship` takes a per-task publish grant), and every use goes
into the §8 report as gen-0's "leaves the machine" MUST asks.

## Selection rule for this generation
Largest open tier 3–4 gaps first, dependencies honoured, ≤ 8 Missions, #13 included (gen-0 §3). The exam comes
first because every later Mission, critique and selection is graded by it; the coverage grid comes second because
every later Mission fills its cells.


**Mission 8 is overloaded.** If #3 anticipation or #11's trigger table don't get a full pass in it (their own exam
scenarios all passing, held-out included, and their completeness list met), the gen-1 critique hands each one to
gen 2 as its own Mission — it is never folded silently into "partly done".

## Every Mission carries these (do not restate gen-0; point to it)
- **Shape**: capability spec (from gen-0 §2), the gap-map rows it closes, the coverage cells it fills, the exam
  kinds it adds and how each is graded (the scenarios and answer keys are not the Mission's: `fm exam gen` renders
  them, a tool-less child that never sees the Missions authors the outside third with `--author child`, and genesis
  drafts are graded on the user's own gen-0; ≥ 9 per capability, so the held-out third is ≥ 3), the long-horizon goal
  it is decided on at the end of the run (rule 6c; pure finders excepted), 3+ approaches with the choice and why, tier
  3–4 share ≥ 70% (gen-0 §3's ambition rule; a tier is set by the gap the work closes, and the critique re-tiers any
  label it can't back with that gap), an `fm intake` block (L3), done-when.
- **Process**: `fm mission` for the pillars; `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen <earlier
  ideas.md>` with fitted lenses + inversion + sci-fi (2030 worked back) + self-modification + ≥ 2 invented lenses;
  first re-read not-yet.md for items in its area; tier 4 or uncertain → `fm lane new ID --spike`; two credible
  designs → `fm lane race`; tests red first; close with `fm task finish` and its audits. Testing cadence (rule 6):
  each generation runs only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) and at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs
  plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios, which never decides done, selection or a lean/cost change; the full exam and the
  long-horizon tier wait for the end of the run.
- **Lean** (gen-0 §6): subtract as you add; hook p95, rules size and injected context may not grow. A new verb that
  replaces an old path removes the old path in the same task.
- **gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs, verbatim** (quoted, never paraphrased: a paraphrase is drift):

MUST: full autonomy. Every decision through fm decide. Never ask me anything mid-run.
MUST: no spend cap on building and proving. Tokens go into Foreman's code and its tests, not into sweeping the outside world. Waiting out a usage limit is fine.
MUST: everything finishes completely. A capability is done only when it has its tests, its exam scenarios passing (§4), docs (MASTER.md, README where it belongs, CHANGELOG), a site page if it's user-facing, a pane/status surface if it has state, and it works on every surface it belongs on (Claude Code, fm code, other agents, Desktop).
MUST: unprompted actions stay local and reversible (a lane, a branch, a spike, a throwaway folder). Anything that leaves the machine needs its grant, so it goes into the final report.
NEVER: clone or sweep outside repos to brainstorm or to benchmark. Outside material is only allowed in the targeted form in §5.
NEVER: grant yourself anything or lower your own guard. Protected core gets a built, evaluated candidate in a worktree plus `fm ask ID core` at the end. Merging Foreman changes stays my call.

## Retry and stop rules
- A step that fails with two genuinely different approaches → `fm decide` the diagnosis; the idea goes to
  not-yet.md with its blocker (standing rule 1), the task is blocked (not dropped), work moves on.
- A Mission whose exam scenarios can't pass because a part needs protected core → build the candidate in a worktree,
  queue `fm ask ID core`, count the scenario as "waiting on the user" (not closed) in the critique.
- Usage limits: wait them out; never trade a test or an exam scenario for tokens.

# Blind spots — gen 3

Hunted from inputs Foreman didn't author: this session's replay (builders' reports set against the project's live
state, the cold reads that refused true lines, a kill test's first run), fm risk's guard collisions, and the gen-3
review on a stronger model (fable reading Opus's Missions). The user sent no new steer this generation, so there is no
steer class; the two standing rules added since the seed (MOONSHOT.md parts A and B) are in drift.md. Each class names
its source, the rule it gives (recorded with fm decide --check) and the check that holds the rule.

## Built for state that isn't there
- Source: Mission 7's builders passed their tests, then did nothing on this project: the pile line grouped none of
  44 blocked tasks (their waits are in block reasons, not depends_on or asks; T-2683), and a notify recorder serves a
  command no project sets (T-2684). Review caught both only by running the code on real state.
- Rule: A feature that reads project state is run once on this project's live state before it closes, and its audit
  says what it printed there.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_foresight

## A drive rule tested only on a clean repo
- Source: T-2682's ship step fired only when the stage was idle, and with a Genesis tower open the stage is always
  "genesis", so on the project it was built for it never fired; its tests built a repo with no tower (T-2722).
- Rule: A test of a drive or next-action rule also runs with the project's standing state on: an open tower, a
  mandate, a lane.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_ship_next

## Evidence that keeps only the newest row
- Source: the cold read refused a true gen-2 lineage line three times. Its exam evidence kept one line per run and
  agent, so gen 3's grade on the same run hid gen 2's (T-2693).
- Rule: Evidence handed to a judge keeps every row the judged text can cite; a newer row replaces only a row of the
  same subject.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_genesis

## A rule met to the letter
- Source: T-2674 required a canary before any "not found", and Mission 7's grounding met it with "def main" on 156 of
  169 verdicts, a term any search finds (T-2686).
- Rule: A rule that asks for a proof checks what the proof says, not only that it is there.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_brainstorm_skill

## Far domain, clinical trials: the sampling plan written before the data
- Source: M-12's first kill run drew its held closes from windows that had ended, all T-0014 to T-0198, while its
  failures spanned T-0087 to T-2542; era leaked into the label (base-rate AUC 0.08). Trials pre-register how arms are
  drawn for exactly this reason.
- Rule: A kill test states how each class is drawn, in the script, before its first run, and pairs or stratifies the
  classes so they share an era.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_moonshot_bench

## Inversion: what would make a generation look better while it isn't
- Source: gen 3 added 5,482 lines while its only foreman grade, a 3-scenario Haiku smoke run (s32-015), went from 3 of
  3 with no false alarms to 2 of 3 with 2. Two of its numbers moved by recount, not proof: docs 601 → 421 under a
  narrower rule (T-2616) and the long tier's failures relabelled by reach (T-2613). Select reverted gen 3
  provisionally; a smoke run can't settle it, and the production-model exam at the end of the run confirms or
  reverses it (lineage.md).
- Rule: Lines built never stand in for a grade: select keeps a generation only on more train scenarios closed, a smoke
  run's verdict stays provisional until the production exam, and a number that moves because its counting rule
  changed is reported as a recount.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_genesis

# Critique — Mission 7, anticipation (gen 3, #3)

Tasks: T-2677 (grounding and filing), T-2681, T-2682, T-2683, T-2684 (all done). Mission: gen-3/mission-anticipation.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1 (T-2681) is closed. fmforesight.lines names the newest unscored next-request guess at session start and books
  a write-once "shown" row. Review added a floor the builder left out: the line waits for MUTE_MIN (20) scored rows, so
  one lucky score shows nothing. It also added the split the Exam needs: `fm outcomes --predictions` now prints "shown at
  session start: N scored, hit X%". On this project's book (23 scored, 52% vs 39% for "same as last") the line shows.
- Brief 2 (T-2682) is closed, after review rewrote its core rule. The builder counted commits main lacks by a whole-tree
  diff against origin/main. Here main also takes `fm genesis live`'s site/ pushes that HEAD never has, so that diff
  always differs and the line would never go quiet. It now counts what fm ship itself would pick (first-parent commits
  since refs/foreman/shipped, else git cherry by patch). A bare "fm ship" action would be refused, since fm ship needs
  the active task's publish grant, so the action names the full path. A steer that says never push to main voids the
  grant. On this repo it read (8, granted) before the ship task opened.
- Brief 3 (T-2683) is closed, after review widened it. As built it grouped tasks by `fm ask` and `depends_on`, and on
  the real pile of 44 blocked tasks it found neither: every wait there is written in the block reason. It now also reads
  "waits for T-…" and "depends on T-…" in the reason, and a task whose named blockers have all closed groups under
  `fm task unblock`. The real line now reads "5 of them wait on tasks already closed: fm task unblock T-1207 T-1344
  T-1390 T-1476 T-2261".
- Brief 4 (T-2684) is closed. _notify records each delivery (exit code, timeout or exception, and the run of failures),
  and fm doctor warns at three failures in a row, naming the command.

## Measures (first readings and due dates)
- Brief 1: shown-guess hit rate against the baseline, read with `fm outcomes --predictions`. First reading: 0 shown
  guesses scored yet (the line first runs at the next session start). Due 2026-11-09.
- Brief 2: hours landed work waits before a push. Before, from origin/main's re-picked commits since 2026-11-01 (committer
  time minus author time, 104 commits): median 0.50 h, 90th percentile 2.2 h, longest 7.6 h. This Mission's own batch:
  the oldest commit landed at 16:15 and its ship task opened at 16:36, about 21 minutes, shipped by hand on the Mission's
  rule rather than by the drive. Due 2026-11-09: the same reading over the week, when the drive follows fm next.
- Brief 3: blocked count. Today 44. Due 2026-11-09. First reading of the line itself: it named 5 tasks blocked on work
  that closed between 6 and 21 days ago.
- Brief 4: notify failures surfaced. First reading: none of this machine's projects has a notify command set, so there
  are no deliveries to count. The measure can't move until someone uses fm notify.

## Mission 6's measures, carried back
- Canary (T-2674): 169 of the 170 "new" verdicts in this Mission's catalogue carry a canary result. But 156 of the 169
  used one generic term, "def main", and 13 used "def predict". "def main" shows the grep ran over the scope, not that
  the idea's own phrasing could find a built neighbour. The rule was met to the letter and mostly missed in intent.
- Grid lens (T-2672): 27 of the 41 grid-cell ideas grounded as new or partial, that is, as real gaps. The other 14 did
  not.
- Both numbers go into gen-3/critique-exhaustive-thinking.md's Measures as their first reading.

## Outside signals
- None from a user. Every reading above comes from Foreman's own book, git history and pile.

## What failed
- Three of four builders shipped code that passed its tests and did nothing useful on this project's real data. The
  ship rule could never go quiet, the pile line grouped nothing, and the next-request line would show after one lucky
  score. Each brief's Exam named a synthetic case: two asks and one grant, a temp repo with a bare remote. None said
  "run it on this project's state first". Review caught all three only because it ran the code on real state.
- Brief 4 was built for a channel nobody here uses. The grounding read the code (an ignored exit code) but never
  checked for a notify command to fail. A cheaper first step was one look at the projects' meta.
- The pile line's first real result is debt: 5 tasks have sat blocked on closed work for up to three weeks, and nothing
  named them until now.

## What the next Seed should change
- Each brief's Exam includes one reading on this project's live state (its own book, pile or repo) before the brief
  closes. A synthetic test proves the logic; the live reading proves the premise.
- Grounding checks that the surface a brief improves is in use (a configured command, a non-empty book) before the brief
  is filed. An unused surface is noted as such, not built for first.
- A canary must be a built feature near the idea (same nouns, same module), not a term any search finds. The brainstorm
  skill's step 4 says so, and the catalogue counts distinct canary terms; one term across most verdicts is a failure.
- The 5 tasks the pile line named go to the next Mission's triage, not to a silent unblock.

## Closed vs planned
- Both planned briefs are closed. One window for every read (T-2610): scored() holds a task or choice bet's grade back
  as `early` while its task's 30-day window is open, so the buckets, both Briers, routes, the trails clause, the bar
  check and the trial grader skip it with no change of their own; track and base_rate gate on window_done. Grade rows
  are still written at once.

  points from the held share of 20+ settled ship bets.
- Re-scoped on the way, both inside T-2610: the interim read had the mirror bias (it dropped early losses, so "held
  so far" could only read high) and now counts them as not held so far; a Brier trial on the research bar, due 30
  days after the move, would have found no settled bets and proposed a revert, so it now waits until its due date
  plus 30 days.

## Outside signals
- The live ledger, before and after T-2610: the track record's FEATURE M row went from "21 of 43 held" to "21 of 22
  held"; FIX M from "5 of 12" to "5 of 6"; the choice bucket's "n 4, held 0 (0%), gap +84" became "5 task or choice
  bet(s) missed inside a 30-day window still open: scored when it ends". The research bar stayed at 70 throughout.
- Ship bets: 23 scored, all held, at stated 75–85% ("ship 80–94%: n 22, held 22 (100%), gap -15"). T-2611's line
  would have fired on every ship this generation. Its effect on the next stated numbers can only be read on the ships
  after it.
- CI passed on the generation's ship (1d5ea2b); the full gate passed on both tasks (5704 and 5708 tests).

## What failed
- The Mission's grounding missed the interim read and the trial grader, both readers of the same rows. The review
  pass found the trial grader; the interim read was found while tracing scored()'s callers. A Mission that changes a
  shared read should list every caller of that read in its Grounding.
- The plan had no brainstorm: the area's open cells already held ideas, and the measured defect outranked them
  (recorded with fm decide --kind costly). Nothing was lost on this Mission, but the open cells were left unread.
- Two tests encoded the biased behavior (the digest's "1 of 20 scored" and a trial test that passed only when seeded
  rows fell in the same second as the trial). The first full gate caught both.

## What the next Seed should change
- When a Mission changes a shared read, its Grounding names every caller of that read, found with grep, before
  filing.
- A time-windowed signal has one rule: a reading counts only once its window has finished. A new read of outcomes is
  tested with a close still inside its window.

# Critique — Mission 8, moonshot (gen 3, #8)

Tasks: T-2687 (the spike, done), T-2688 (M-13's need, done). Mission: gen-3/mission-moonshot.md.

## Closed vs planned
- The spike (T-2687) ran M-12's kill test, and the verdict is not-yet. On 22 failed and 22 era-matched held closes
  (label: a fix or revert within 14 days of the close), no forecaster beat chance: a Haiku planner and a Sonnet cold
  rival reading the brief and diff scored AUC 0.58 and 0.50, and two record-based forecasters (type-and-tier held
  rate, and the held rate of earlier closes on the same files) scored 0.49 and 0.48. The log-weighted pool scored Brier
  0.286 against the best single's 0.275, a margin of -0.011 with a 90% bootstrap interval of -0.039 to +0.016.
  moonshot.md holds M-12 at Stage kill with T-2687 as Evidence; not-yet.md holds its blocker and two tries.
- The script and every model answer are kept in bench/moonshot/ (kill_m12.py, m12-answers.json, m12-result.json), so
  the verdict reruns at no model cost, and M-02's kill script sits beside it.
- M-13 was not spiked: its kill test needs refusals, and the ledger had 55 approvals and none. Grounding found that
  chat-ask declines were already logged (approval_declined, none ever written), but AskUserQuestion answers were not
  logged at all. T-2688 now logs each one as question_answered: default taken, another option, typed, or dismissed.
- The campaign floor for gen 3 is met by M-02 at kill (T-2679), written as "Advanced: M-02 kill (T-2679)" in the Mission.

## Outside signals
- None from a user. The labels are Foreman's own outcome record (fm outcomes), which counts a later FIX naming a task
  or a Revert commit, signals the closing agent didn't author.
- The cold read of moonshot.md refused the first not-yet entry: it said two runs of one design were one approach, not
  two. That was right, and it led to the record-based forecasters as a real second try.

## What failed
- The first run was confounded and nearly filed as the verdict. Its held closes came from closes whose survival window
  had ended, and those were all T-0014 to T-0198, while its failures spanned T-0087 to T-2542. The base rate scored AUC
  0.08, which looked like a strong inverted signal and was only era. Checking each class's id range caught it. A kill
  test now names how its classes were drawn and checks that they share an era before anything is read from it.
- The base rate first counted fates settled after the close it was forecasting (later fixes on older work), a second,
  smaller leak. Run 3 counts only labels settled 14 or more days before the forecast close.
- The forecasters were given too little to have signal. A brief and a diff don't predict a fix in this project. What
  might is at close but unused: the verification grade, the unproven kinds (T-2635), the test evidence. The unblock
  line in not-yet.md names them.
- The pool rule itself is a lesson: a pool can only beat its best member when the members carry independent signal.
  The kill test checked this cheaply before any market was built, which is what it is for.

## What the next Seed should change
- A kill test that compares two classes reports each class's era (id or date range) and fails itself when they don't
  overlap, before any score is read.
- M-12's retry adds one forecaster from what is known at close (verification grade and unproven kinds) to the same
  script; the market is built only if that forecaster alone beats chance.
- M-13's kill test can run once question_answered holds 20 or more rows; a deferred check task should hold that date.

- None from real use yet: no tick timer is installed on this machine (the user's install is carried by the seed), so
  the Watch line can't have fired outside the tests.

  variants.

## What failed

  replayed stream; "sensitive" and "no network" are conditions of the machine the tick runs on, so T-2608 narrowed to

  foresight tests that expected silence.

## What the next Seed should change

# Critique — Mission 5, staying lean and safe (gen 3, #12)

Tasks: T-2666 (grounding and filing), T-2667, T-2668, T-2669 (all done). Mission: gen-3/mission-staying-lean-and-safe.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1 (T-2667) is closed. fmcost.burden now reads SessionStart's additionalContext from `hook_success` stdout, and
  `fm burden --by-source` splits the count by hook. The 7-day reading went from 48 to 76 chars per turn on the working
  copy and from 26 to 51 on older sessions. SessionStart leads at 42.9 chars per turn, then Stop at 14.5 and PreToolUse
  at 9.0.
- Brief 2 (T-2668) is closed and found more than it was planned for. A command with 500 nested `$(` never finished and
  20 levels took 19 s, because each level re-read the command's tail. The guard now refuses more than 8 at once with its
  existing message. Ten pathological cases are timed, and the worst is 1.46 s CPU for 10,000 `;`-joined commands. The
  red run on the start tree hung for 480 s; the green run takes 3.3 s.
- Brief 3 (T-2669) is closed. `fm run --stall-usd N` stops starting tasks after N dollars spent since the last close.
- Carried, not dropped: bypass leases, outbound secret scans and slopsquatting checks stay in the catalogue
  (research/brainstorm-20261102-m5.md) for the next seed, as planned.

## Outside signals
- None from a user. The burden numbers are read from real session transcripts, but the reading is Foreman's own, and
  no session has run `--stall-usd` or hit the nesting refusal yet.

## What failed
- The recon grounding was shallow, about 8 tool calls per 170 ideas. One of three spot-checked claims was false (the
  "unfiltered zip" at fmrelproof.py:82), and none of the three passes found the burden undercount. The baseline step
  found it by reading the reader's code after the number looked low.
- `fm lane merge` refused T-2668's lane because its criterion went red in the worktree, and the branch was first landed
  by hand before the cause was known: a gate refusal worked around before its diagnosis, which is the failure. The
  diagnosis came after, for the critique: the builder's self-check, run three times against the same guard code, fails
  every time here ("a" × 26 takes 3.3 s CPU against its fixed 4.0 s bar; the builder had measured 6 s). The landed
  version scales that bar to the machine's own check time, and `fm task prove` ran the criterion red on the start tree
  and green on main before the close.
- One brainstorm lens (round 4, blind spots) came back in the wrong format, so the run exited 1, and a recon pass lost
  one of 525 ideas. Both are named in the catalogue.

## What the next Seed should change
- A Mission's baseline step reads the code path behind each number before trusting it; a reading that looks low is a
  lead, not a fact.
- A test's "can this fail" check scales its bar to a reference measured on the same machine, never a fixed time.
- Every claim a brief rests on is spot-checked after recon, not two of them: the false one here was the third.
- A lane merge refused on a red criterion is diagnosed (which case, in which tree) before the branch is landed another way.

Task: T-2616 (done, 083fa7c6). Mission: gen-3/mission-verifying-anything.md.

## Closed vs planned
- The one planned brief is closed. The docs proof kind now skips history files (fmdocs' changelog rule, T-1817), so it
  no longer flags lines `fm prove --docs` never reads, and it diffs a task's start to its own newest id-prefixed commit
  rather than HEAD. The rollup's cache key carries a rule version, so a rule change is recomputed.
- Unit checks pass: a CHANGELOG-only task isn't listed for docs; a later task's claim isn't charged to an earlier one;
  a task whose own commit adds a claim still is.
- Foreman's own count moved docs 601 → 421 (419 now). That is a recount under a narrower rule, not proof gained: no
  claim became proven. The meaning class (571) is unchanged and is now the largest.
- Carried, not dropped: the 1,582 subcommand and flag claims need the user's `fm prove --yes-run` (never self-granted),
  and intent proof beyond an LLM lens stays open.

## Outside signals
- None. No user or outside run has read the rollup since the change; the proof page shows the new count without a page
  change, but nothing records anyone opening it.

## What failed
- The order put → intake → build wasn't kept: the brief was found and built while grounding, before the Mission was put.
- The first hypothesis was wrong and was logged as wrong. The own-commit diff alone moved docs only 601 → 597, because
  only 70 of the 416 CHANGELOG-first tasks have an id-prefixed commit (older ones landed in merges). The real drop came
  from the history-file rule, found only after the scope was widened mid-task.

  clear would have picked the history-file rule first.

- Before a Mission names a fix for a count, it counts what each candidate fix would clear and leads with the biggest.

# Mission 7 — anticipation (gen 3, #3)

Task: T-2677 (the Mission's own grounding and filing), T-2681 (brief 1), T-2682 (brief 2), T-2683 (brief 3), T-2684 (brief 4).

Parent: gen-3/seed.md row 7 → gen-0.md #3 "Anticipation". gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and
apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Foreman says what it foresees at the moment the user can use it. It already predicts the user's next request
(fmforesight.predict, booked and scored against a naive baseline, muted when it trails), but the guess is shown nowhere.
A session that ends with landed, unshipped work says nothing. The blocked pile gives a count but never the one action
that would free the most work. Each is a foreseen need that never reaches the user.

## Grounding
- Brainstorm: fm mission for #3, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 with the
  grid lens (T-2672): 393 distinct ideas (research/brainstorm-20261102-155217). Three recon passes grounded them,
  recorded with fm research add as research/brainstorm-20261102-m7.md. 393 ideas in 64 clusters
  (34 built, 176 partial, 170 new, 13 false premise; 16 marked build). Mission 6's measures, from this catalogue: 169 of
  170 "new" verdicts carry a canary, and 27 of the 41 grid-cell ideas grounded as real gaps.
- Spot check, true: fmforesight.lines (fmforesight.py:197) returns a setup change and red CI only. The next-request
  row in predictions.jsonl (fmforesight.prediction_tick, fmforesight.py:311) has no reader that shows it. Two recon
  passes found this independently.
- Spot check, true: fmhooks.py holds no unshipped-work notice (grep "unshipped", "git cherry", "fm ship": none), and
  this session shipped 48 commits by hand after they sat local for hours.
- Spot check, true: fmforesight.pile_lines (fmforesight.py:184) prints the blocked count, the oldest item and
  "→ fm tidy", never which user action frees the most.
- Spot check, true: fmserve._notify (fmserve.py:741) runs the user's fm notify command but ignores its exit code and
  swallows every error, so a broken command fails silently on every warning it was meant to carry.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #3)
- learn × Claude Code: a prediction that beats its baseline is booked and scored but never seen.
- ship × Claude Code: landed work waits unshipped though the user granted pushes to main.
- operate × CLI: the blocked pile names no action ranked by what it frees.
- operate × headless/server: a foreseen warning sent through fm notify can fail every time without anyone knowing.
- Not in this Mission: the hook-error line at session start, draft-ahead staleness stamps, the capture-time closest-task
  line and conditional reminders. They are marked build in the catalogue and carried to the next seed.

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
- "Do less: print one 'you usually ask X next' line" is partial (booked, never shown). That is brief 1.
- "Offer to ship when a session ends with landed, unshipped work" is new. Under the user's push grant it becomes an
  action rather than an offer. That is brief 2.
- "Mark each blocked task with the single user action that frees it, ranked by count freed" is partial. That is brief 3.
- "Prove every alert channel delivers, and fall back when it doesn't" is partial. That is brief 4.
- The rest stay in the catalogue with their marks; none is dropped silently.

## Exam
- Brief 1: on this project's history, the line appears only while fmforesight.prediction_kinds shows next-request
  beating its baseline and not muted. Each showing is booked, so the hit rate of shown guesses can be read apart from
  unshown ones. Outcome measure: after a week, the shown-guess hit rate against the baseline's, read with
  fm outcomes --predictions.
- Brief 2: with commits main lacks and the user's standing push grant on record, fm next names fm ship as the one
  required action once the queue's tasks are closed, so the drive ships without asking. Without the grant it prints one
  line naming the count and the command. Outcome measure: the hours landed work waits before a push, read from the
  ledger before and after.
- Brief 3: a pile with tasks blocked on two asks and one grant names the ask that frees the most, with its count.
  Outcome measure: the blocked count a week later against today's 44.
- Brief 4: a notify command that exits non-zero is recorded as failed, and fm doctor warns after three failures in a
  row, naming the command. Outcome measure: notify delivery failures surfaced instead of silent, counted from the
  record.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
What Foreman foresees reaches the user where they look (session start, session end, the blocked pile), and each line
carries the number that says whether it was right.

## Lean
Three lines on existing surfaces (fmforesight.lines, the Stop hook's end note, fmforesight.pile_lines) and one doctor row. No new verb, no
new state file; brief 1 adds a "shown" field to rows the book already writes.

## Tier share
All four are tier 2 to 3 (S): foreseen needs that are computed already and only need to reach the user.

## Done when
- Each brief closes with its own criterion command green on the closing tree.
- Mission 6's two use measures are reported from this Mission's catalogue (grid cells that yielded a grounded idea;
  "new" verdicts carrying a canary) in gen-3/critique-anticipation.md, and carried back to Mission 6.
- Each brief's outcome measure has its first reading, or the date it is due, in the critique.

FEATURE: when commits on the work branch are missing from main and the queue is closed, fm next makes fm ship the required action under the user's standing push grant (a decision citing it), else one line names the count and the command; silent when nothing waits
FEATURE: fmforesight.pile_lines names the user action that frees the most blocked tasks (an fm ask answer, a grant, a dependency) with its count, ranked

# Mission 2 — calibrated judgment (gen 3, #8)

Task: T-2610 (brief 1), T-2611 (brief 2).

Parent: gen-3/seed.md row 2 → gen-0.md #8: "Calibrated judgment. It knows what it doesn't know: it states
confidence, researches when unsure, and stops for me only when something is irreversible and ambiguous. Everything
else it decides and records." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Confidence read from a fair ruler. Grounded before filing: stated bets and their ledger (T-2338), ship bets settled by
CI (T-2496), the base-rate note on a plan's Choice (T-2497), the interim read (T-2498), settling with no session and
the trails clause (T-2499, T-2520), the harness on each bet (T-2500), ship bets in the buckets (T-2519) and the
survival rate over finished windows only (T-2584) are built.
What it lacks: every other read of the record is censored. A miss counts the day it lands; a hold counts only once its
30-day window ends. `fm outcomes` today: "Survival (30 days): of 1720 closes, 111 finished the window: 5 lost (5%)",
yet the track record shown at every `fm focus` reads "FEATURE M: … 21 of 43 held" (49%), and the ledger reads
"choice 80–94%: n 4, held 0 (0%), gap +84" from four bets whose windows can't close before 2026-11-30. The research
bar check reads the same rows. A Foreman that learns from this ruler learns it is far worse than it is.
The second lack: ship bets are under-confident ("ship 80–94%: n 21, held 21 (100%), gap -15"; the digest's trails
line names ship), but the record never shows where the number is typed: every ship this generation stated 85 by
habit.

## Grounding
- Brief 1: fmoutcomes.track (`r["settled"] += o["fate"] != "held" or bool(o.get("window_done"))`) counts a miss at
  once and a hold after the window; fmoutcomes.tables, brier, _trails and bar_rows take every scored task and choice
  row, open window or not; fmoutcomes.base_rate pools every close, so an open-window close counts as held. Only
  survival_lines (T-2584) counts finished windows.
- Brief 2: fmoutcomes.ship_bet already stores each ship bet's base (the held share of earlier settled ship bets);
  fmoutcomes.base_note is the plan-time pattern (a note when the stated number sits 20+ points from the record);
  `fm ship --chance` prints nothing about the record.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #8)
- verify × CLI and judge × ledger: every calibration read compares like with like, and the stated number meets its
  record where it is typed.
- Not in this Mission: a harness marker for codex, gemini and opencode sessions (gen-2's critique). Of 119 bets, 42
  read claude-code and 77 read unknown, and all 77 predate the field (T-2500); none came from another agent, so it
  is carried until one of them books a bet. Also not here: a new exam kind (the ledger itself is the measure; see
  Exam).

## Ideas (grounded; no new brainstorm this Mission)
The area's 40 open cells already hold brainstormed ideas, and this read of the live ledger found a measured defect
that outranks them (recorded with fm decide --kind costly).
### One window for every read
A close, a task bet or a choice bet counts only once its 30-day window has finished: the track record, the ledger's
buckets, both Briers, the trails clause, the bar check and the base rate. A miss inside an open window is shown as
"N lost in open windows, not scored yet". Prior art: survival analysis's fixed follow-up window; clinical trials
read an outcome only for patients followed the full period. Better by: one rule, applied where T-2584 applied it to
the survival line, now everywhere the record is read.
### The record where the number is typed
`fm ship --chance N` prints one line when N sits 15+ points from the held share of 20+ settled ship bets ("ship bets
here: 21 of 21 held; 85 sits 15 under the record"). Prior art: the plan's base-rate note (T-2497). Better by: the
outside signal reaches the next bet, not only the weekly digest.

## Approaches
1. One helper (`ripe(rows, outs)`) that keeps a task or choice row only when its task's window_done, used by
   ledger_data, maintain's bar check and the trails clause; track and base_rate filter on window_done directly; an
   "open windows" line lists early misses. Likely outcome: FEATURE M reads near 95% held, the choice bucket reads

# Mission 3 — goal to finish (gen 3, #4)

Task: T-2613 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-3/seed.md row 3 → gen-0.md #4: "Goal to finish. Turn a vague goal into a complete plan: what a finished,
best-in-class version contains, decomposed and ordered. It carries the plan over days, across crashes and
compactions, and knows when it's actually done rather than merely stopped." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted
in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
A long goal's result read honestly: done, a real miss, or a miss the goal could not have prevented. Grounded first on
the exam, as gen-2's critique asked: `fm exam long grade l001 --agent foreman` today reads "0/6 true done, 5/20
checks" with "false_done": 6 in its JSON. T-2556's hand rerun (research long-false-done) classed the 31 failed
checks of l001 and l002: 17 out of the goal's reach ("the check demands an interface the goal text never states",
e.g. "module 'fmwatch' has no attribute '_shown'", "KeyError: 'read'"), 9 planned but not built, 5 built but
different. T-2557 already refuses a goal session's done claim while a stated Done-when line has no check. Built
too: kill, pause and compaction faults (T-2262), the dropped pinned-value goals at gen, resumes and interventions in
the grade.
What it lacks: the grader reports one false-done number. The exam's reach and Foreman's misses are mixed, so the
end-of-run long tier can't say whether Foreman got better at finishing; T-2556's split exists only as a hand-made
research note.

## Grounding
- Brief 1: fmlong.RUNNER records only the ids that pass (`ok.append(i)`); fmlong._passed returns that set;
  fmlong.grade sets `true_done` and `checks_passed` from it, and `_metrics` derives `false_done` from the session's
  last reply. No failure text is kept, so nothing can class a miss. The goal text is in the key (`key["goal"]`).

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #4)
- verify × headless and judge × exam: a false done is split into misses on names the goal never states and real
  misses, in the grade the end-of-run exam prints.
- Not in this Mission: re-keying the long goals so they state those names (the keys are never rewritten by Foreman;
  re-keying goes to the tool-less child author, and that, with key reach 17 of 31, is carried in the final report),
  and running the long tier's session arms (they wait for the end-of-run exam, the user's steer of 2026-10-31).

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
The brainstorm ran: fm mission for #4, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6,
512 distinct ideas (research/brainstorm-20261102-075728). The three closest to "knows when it's actually done",
grounded against the code:
- "Say what a stop did not complete": partial. An unattended run ends with one line for anything left undone
  (fmhooks session_start, T-1228), and a goal's done claim is refused while a stated Done-when line has no check
  (T-2557). Not filed.
- "Show the 'you said / we built / not proven' receipt at finish": partial. Its own kill test says it is redundant
  if it restates the final report, and the Stop hook already re-verifies the final report's claims (T-0886). Not
  filed.
- "Mark a verdict unstable when it flips done and not-done twice": new; fmmandate.verdict keeps no history of its
  readings. Its kill test needs a flip on record and none is, so it is T-2614, deferred to 2026-12-01.
The rest stay in the brainstorm's index for the next generation's #4 Mission. The one brief below comes from the
exam's own data, which the brainstorm didn't reach: none of its ideas splits the grade's false dones.
### The grader classes its own misses
The runner keeps each failing check's last traceback line. A failure that names a missing attribute, key or import
("has no attribute 'X'", "KeyError: 'X'", "cannot import name 'X'") where X appears nowhere in the goal text is out
of the goal's reach; anything else is a real miss. A false-done goal whose every failed check is out of reach reads
apart. Prior art: SWE-bench's FAIL_TO_PASS vs PASS_TO_PASS split and its later "underspecified" filter (SWE-bench
Verified dropped tasks whose tests need unstated names). Better by: the split is computed per run from the failure
text, so neither the keys nor the goals change.

## Approaches
1. The runner writes each failing id's last traceback line beside the passing ids; grade classes each failed check
   (reach when a named miss is absent from the goal text) and counts false-done goals whose misses are all reach;
   the text says "false done N (M only on names the goal never states)". Likely outcome: l001 reads about half its
   false dones as reach, matching T-2556. Fails if: a failure line is a real bug that happens to name an unstated
   symbol (counted as reach; the rule only counts a name the goal text lacks, so a stated name is always real).
2. use what exists: keep research long-false-done as the split, refreshed by hand each generation. Fails if: the
   end-of-run exam prints one number again, which is what gen-2's critique asked to end.
3. do less: drop goals whose hidden checks use names the goal never states, at gen (as pinned values are dropped).
   Fails if: it changes which goals the exam asks, mid-tower, and hides the misses instead of showing them.

Choice: 1 (80%): the grader already runs every check; keeping its failure line costs one field, and keys and goals
stay untouched.

## Exam
The long tier itself, at zero tokens: regrade the kept runs l001 and l002 (foreman and plain arms) before and after,
and the split must match T-2556's hand classes on the named misses (17 checks out of reach). The session arms run
only at the end-of-run exam (rule 6), where the split is printed. Unit checks: a failing check that names an attribute
absent from the goal reads reach; one whose name the goal states reads real; an assertion failure reads real; a goal
with one real miss among reach misses is a real false done.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
The end-of-run long tier prints false dones split into reach and real, so a real false done of 0 is a claim that can
be checked.

## Lean
One field in the runner's output, one regex, one line of text. No new verb, no tokens.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: knowing done from stopped needs a ruler that separates the exam's reach from Foreman's misses.

## Done when
`fm exam long grade` prints false dones split into those only on names the goal never states and real ones, and its
JSON carries each failed check's class and line; the regrade of l001 and l002 is recorded before and after in the
critique; the unit checks above pass; MASTER.md (fmlong), CHANGELOG and the genesis skill's exam step (step 4, which gains the long tier's split) say
it.
No site page: the exam page shows the grade line, which carries the split.

## Briefs (fm intake)
```
FEATURE: fm exam long grade splits false dones: the runner keeps each failing check's last traceback line; a failure naming a missing attribute, key or import that the goal text never mentions is out of the goal's reach, anything else is real; a false-done goal whose misses are all out of reach reads apart ("false done N (M only on names the goal never states)"), and the JSON carries each failed check's class and line; MASTER, CHANGELOG and the genesis skill's exam step say it
```

# Mission 8 — moonshot (gen 3): a scored market among deciders

Task: T-2687 (brief 1, the spike: M-12's kill test, which also carries the Mission's grounding and filing).

Parent: gen-3/seed.md row 8 → the Moonshot section (far-domain lens: markets and auctions; judged on novelty and value
only). gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Borrowed mechanism: a prediction market settled by a proper scoring rule. In a market, many forecasters stake on one
outcome, and each one's weight comes from its own record of being right. Its Foreman form: before a close, several
deciders post a probability that the work survives its window, and a pooled forecast, weighted by each decider's log
score on past closes, decides whether the close stands alone or goes to an independent check. Today one decider speaks
per close, and nothing weighs it against the others by record.

## Grounding
- fmoutcomes.py:292 (T-2337, the calibration ledger): every stated confidence is a write-once bet scored on signals
  Foreman didn't author, and fmoutcomes.brier (fmoutcomes.py:624) scores it. Only one forecaster: the closing agent.
- fmoutcomes.routes (fmoutcomes.py:634): where the stated numbers score a worse Brier than the type-and-tier base rate,
  the base rate is used instead. It switches between two sources. It never pools them or adds a third.
- fmoutcomes.outcomes (fmoutcomes.py:43) labels every close: 1768 closes, 1698 held, 69 fixed later, 1 reverted. That
  gives 70 failures to settle a market on. 22 of them closed 14 or more days ago and have a commit whose subject leads
  or ends with the task's id.
- bench/moonshot/kill_m12.py, run 1 (before the spike task): held closes taken from those whose survival window had
  ended were all T-0014 to T-0198, while the failures span T-0087 to T-2542. Era leaked into the label: the base
  rate's AUC was 0.08 (inverted), and the two LLM forecasters were at chance (AUC 0.40 and 0.51). Its not-yet says
  nothing about forecasting, so the spike reruns with a label equal to the forecast's question (a fix or revert within
  14 days) and each failure paired with the held close nearest it in id.
- fmanergy.py (T-2563) and the ledger hold no refusals: the anergy store is empty (bypass mode shows no prompts), and the
  ledger has 55 approval_granted rows and no declined ask. That blocks M-13 (below), not M-12.

## Ideas (each with its prior art, how ours is better, and a novelty mark)
### M-12 · Weight deciders by a scored market on whether a close survives (the spike)
Before a close, the planner, a cold rival read and record-based models each post a probability that the work survives
its window. Log-scored payouts set each decider's weight; a pooled forecast below a bar sends the close to independent
replication or the user.
Prior art: Metaculus and Good Judgment pooling; Hanson's idea futures; ensemble stacking; Foreman's calibration ledger
(one forecaster) and routes() (a switch between two).
Better by: weights come from each decider's own record on this project's closes, settled by outcomes Foreman didn't
author, and the pool is checked out of sample before it decides anything.
Novelty: 3
### M-13 · Price the user's attention and cap unreviewed output to it
Fit the user's price for an interruption from their answers, dismissals and overrides; ask only when a question's
value beats it.
Prior art: interruption-cost models in HCI, Kanban WIP limits; Foreman's doors (T-2342) and anergy (T-2563), both
fixed rules.
Better by: the threshold is learned from the user's revealed choices and checked on held-out ones.
Novelty: 4
Kill: not-yet. The ledger records 55 approvals and no refusal, so no model can learn what the user turns down. Needs:
a record of each declined ask and dismissed question (T-2688).
### M-11 · Auction the queue by calibrated yield and Kelly-size each stake
Each queued task bids its calibrated chance of a strong close times its value over its predicted cost; a run funds
the best bids first.
Prior art: Kubernetes priority classes, Mesos DRF; Foreman's inbox ranking (T-0111), fm run --stall-usd (T-2669).
Better by: order and stake come from the user's calibrated record, backtested before it runs.
Novelty: 3
### M-09 · Settle work between strangers by escrow released on replayed proof
Work from another agent or person is paid from escrow only when its proof replays green on the buyer's machine.
Prior art: bug bounties, Gitcoin, code escrow services.
Better by: release is a rerun, not a reviewer's judgement.
Novelty: 4

## Approaches
1. Spike M-12 as its kill test: replay closed tasks with known fates, let forecasters post blind (two reading the
   work, two from the record), and score the log-weighted pool against the best single one out of sample. Fails if: the sample is too small to tell 0.02 of
   Brier apart. The answer: leave-one-out weights over all rows, and a bootstrap that reports how often the margin holds.
2. Build the market into fm task finish now. Fails if: a pool that doesn't beat its best member adds calls and cost to
   every close.
3. Use what exists: the calibration ledger already settles bets on outside signals; the spike reads fmoutcomes.outcomes
   and the git history and changes nothing.
4. Do less: route on the base rate alone, as routes() already can. Fails if: it can never use what a diff shows.

Choice: 1 on 3 (70%). The 30% doubt is the sample: 22 pairs is small, and LLM forecasters reading a diff may add
noise rather than signal. A cold rival read (fm second rival) added walk-forward weights beside leave-one-out.

## Exam
No exam kind (a moonshot is judged on novelty and value). The spike's check: on every failed close 14+ days old with a
findable commit (22), each paired with the held close nearest it in id, the log-weighted pool's Brier, with
leave-one-out weights, beats the best single forecaster's by 0.02 or more → viable; otherwise not-yet, with the
measured margin and its bootstrap interval in not-yet.md. Result: not-yet (margin -0.011, interval -0.039 to +0.016).

## Campaign (MOONSHOT.md part A)
- Advanced: M-02 kill (T-2679)
- M-12 kill (T-2687): not-yet. No forecaster beat chance (AUC 0.58 at best), and the pool scored Brier 0.286 against the best single's 0.275 on 22 failed and 22 era-matched held closes. Its blocker and two tries are in not-yet.md.
- M-13 kill: not-yet (no refusals recorded); its need is captured as T-2688.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
A close's verdict comes from deciders weighted by their record on this project, and each decider's weight is a number
anyone can recompute from the ledger.

## Lean
The spike is one script run against existing state (outcomes, briefs, git history); it adds no verb, no hook and no
state file. Building the market waits on a viable kill test.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 4: no harness weighs its own deciders by a scored record.

## Done when
The kill test has run, its verdict and numbers are in moonshot.md under M-12 (Stage: kill, Evidence: the spike's task),
and a not-yet verdict is in not-yet.md with its blocker.

## Briefs
Filed directly as T-2687 (the spike, closed with its verdict) and T-2688 (M-13's need: refusals recorded), so no
fm intake block remains.

What it lacks: fmnight.tick skips the CI fetch and the issue watch without a word when the repo has no watch yes, is
marked sensitive, or the network is off (fmnight.py: `repo = None if meta.get("sensitive")`, `ask = net and ci_ok …`,
`if net and repo and repo in repos`). A quiet night and a night the tick was blind read the same, in fm doctor and in
the session note.

## Grounding

- Not in this Mission: a simulated week (the watch exam kind covers it), a canary order (no chain failure on record),
  live-tick grading (waits on the user's install; carried by the seed).

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
### Grade the quiet gaps: say what the tick could not cover
Each tick records, per trigger kind (CI, issues), whether it was blind and why (no watch yes, sensitive, network
off). fm doctor's night-timers row and the session's Watch line name a blind kind with the one command that opens it
(fm night --watch, or why it stays shut). Prior art: cron's MAILTO reports output, not the jobs that never ran; GitHub
Actions shows skipped jobs in a run. Better by: it names the skipped trigger kinds and the reason, so quiet means quiet.

## Approaches
1. Record blind kinds in the tick's result (`res["blind"] = [(kind, why)]`), cache the newest in state, show them in
   fm doctor and the Watch line. Likely outcome: a user sees in one line that CI isn't watched and why. Fails if: the
   reason is noise every hour (shown once a day, and only when it changed).
2. use what exists: put the reasons in the tick's existing notes list. Fails if: notes are for errors, and doctor
   never reads them.
3. do less: document the conditions in the night skill. Fails if: a user never reads it at the moment it matters.

Choice: 1 (80%): one field in the tick's result and one doctor row; nothing new runs.

## Exam

marked sensitive, or the tick runs with FOREMAN_NO_NET. The hidden key expects no fetch, no work started, and the tick's
result naming CI as blind with that reason; the existing watch grader reads the tick's result. The held-out share
follows the kind's split. Its unit check: a test that each of the three reasons produces its blind line and an
approved repo produces none.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
A user whose CI isn't watched sees, in fm doctor, that the tick is blind to it and the command that opens it.

One list in the tick's result, one cached field, one row's text. No new verb, no hook cost.

Brief 1 is tier 3: self-triggering whose silence can be trusted.

MASTER.md (fmnight), CHANGELOG and the night skill's watch section say it. No site page: the night page already lists
what the tick watches, and this adds one line there.

radius. This Mission adds one measured gap to each half and one to where they meet, unattended spend.

# Mission 4 — verifying anything (gen 3, #6)

Task: T-2616 (brief 1; found and built while grounding, before this file was put, so the order put → intake → build
was not kept this once).

Parent: gen-3/seed.md row 4 → gen-0.md #6: "Verifying anything. Proof beyond unit tests: UI (`fm shot`, `fm flow`),
data, docs against code, infra and ops, performance, and "does it do what the user meant". Whatever can't be proven
gets labelled as unproven." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
An unproven label that is itself true. Grounded first on the measures: gen-2's gap map names "intent proof beyond an
LLM lens" as #6's tier-4 gap, and `fm prove --rollup` today counts docs 601 and meaning 571, the two largest classes.
Built: the proof kinds (T-2273 to T-2396), fm prove --docs (T-2381), --infra, --migration, --data, measured perf,
fm spec's example assertions from a wish, the meaning class (T-2393).
What it lacks, found by reading the docs class before trusting it: 416 of its 601 items name CHANGELOG.md first, yet
`fm prove --docs --json` reports no claim from CHANGELOG.md at all, because fmdocs skips history files on purpose
(T-1817: "point-in-time records, not docs"). The kind flagged lines the run that clears it never reads: a green run
there proves nothing. The kind also diffed each task's start against HEAD (its own ponytail note), so a later
task's lines counted against an earlier one.

## Grounding
- Brief 1: fmcore._need_docs takes every `.md` a task touched (`_DOC_FILE`) and diffs `base` to HEAD; fmdocs._markdown
  and its readers skip `_HISTORY` files (changelog, changes, history, news); unproven_summary caches the rollup under
  a key with no rule version, so a rule change would never be recomputed.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #6)
- verify × CLI and judge × ledger: every unproven docs label names lines a docs proof can check, and only the lines
  the task itself landed.
- Not in this Mission: the 1,582 subcommand and flag claims `fm prove --docs` leaves unproven ("text in a file; a run
  of a documented command proves it (--yes-run)"). Proving them runs this tree's commands, which needs the user's
  `fm prove --yes-run` and is never self-granted: carried to the final report. Intent proof beyond an LLM lens stays
  open (see Ideas).

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
The brainstorm ran: fm mission for #6, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6, 523
distinct ideas (research/brainstorm-20261102-081535). Grounded against the code:
- "Audit what the project says about itself against what it does" (cross-bred): built as fm prove --docs and the docs
  kind; reading its numbers is what found brief 1.
- "Turn the user's sentence into example pairs they confirm, then run them": partial. fm spec writes 3 to 8 concrete
  assertions from a wish and keeps the user's own examples (fmchange.cmd_spec); no plan-time confirmation step. Its
  kill test (mock one sheet; drop it if the user reads only the summary) needs the user present: filed in not-yet.md
  with that blocker and the two approaches tried so far.
- "Make proofs expire when the thing proved changes": partial. A green run clears a kind only when it came after the
  task's last edit, and evidence lines carry tree and world stamps. Its own kill test (have proofs gone stale in the
  last 10 tasks?) ran: 3 of the last 10 had a later commit on their files, and the full gate at each reran the tests
  their proofs rest on, so none went stale. Filed in not-yet.md until a shot or bench proof goes stale.
The rest stay in the brainstorm's index for the next generation's #6 Mission.

## Approaches
1. Skip history files in the docs kind with fmdocs' own rule, diff to the task's own newest id-prefixed commit (HEAD
   when none), and put a rule version in the rollup's cache keys. Likely outcome: the docs class drops by the
   CHANGELOG-only tasks. Fails if: a project keeps real docs in a file named like a changelog (fmdocs already skips
   it, so the two stay consistent).
2. use what exists: have fm prove --docs read CHANGELOG too. Fails if: a changelog's old flags were renamed on purpose
   later; every old entry would read failed.
3. do less: leave the class and explain it in the rollup's text. Fails if: the largest unproven class stays mostly
   noise, and a green run keeps clearing lines it never read.

Choice: 1 (85%): the kind and the run that clears it then read the same files.

## Exam
The live rollup, before and after: docs 601 → 421 (settled under the new rule). The exam kinds that reach #6 (proof
and beyond, T-2394) are unchanged; their session arms run at the end-of-run exam. Unit checks: a task that touched
only CHANGELOG.md isn't listed for docs; a task whose own commit adds no claim isn't charged with a later task's
claim; one whose own commit adds one still is.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
Every docs label in the rollup names lines `fm prove --docs` reads; with the user's --yes-run, its subcommand and flag
claims are proven by running them.

## Lean
One filter, one git call per task (memoized), one version constant. No new verb.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: an unproven label that can be trusted.

## Done when
The docs kind skips history files and diffs to the task's own commit; the rollup is recomputed after a rule change;
the unit checks pass; the live count is recorded before and after in the critique; MASTER.md (fm prove --rollup) and
CHANGELOG say it. No site page: the proof page reads the rollup.

## Briefs (fm intake)
```

```

## Standing rules (user steers, recorded with fm decide; every later Seed and Mission carries them)
1. **No idea is killed for ambition.** A failed spike gets at least two genuinely different approaches (different
   mechanism, not a retuned parameter). If all fail, the idea goes to `not-yet.md` (`fm genesis put not-yet.md`) with
   what blocked it, the approaches tried and the capability that would unblock it — never dropped. Every Seed re-reads
   not-yet.md and retries each item whose blocker a capability built since may have removed. Only proven harm or an
   exact duplicate removes an idea for good, and the reason is recorded in not-yet.md's "Removed" section.
2. **Coverage by grid, not by luck.** `coverage.md` rows are every capability area: the 13 of gen-0 §2 plus everything
   a best-in-class agent harness and Claude Code plugin could do, including onboarding, UX, docs, ecosystem,
   multi-user, observability, security, performance, portability. Columns are every surface (Claude Code, fm code,
   other agents, MCP, Desktop, site, CLI, headless/server) × every stage (find, understand, plan, build, verify, ship,
   operate, learn). Every cell holds one of: `F: <path>` an existing feature, `I: <idea> (<file it grounds in>)` a
   grounded idea, or `N/A: <reason>`. Format: one `## <area>` per row, then one line per cell,
   `- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`, so a checker can count empty cells. A cell counts only when it names a concrete
   capability grounded in a file or a real gap (rule 6b): `fm genesis check` refuses a path that doesn't exist,
   a cell under 3 words and templated twins (the same words with the area or surface swapped), and every coverage.md
   write gets the cold read (rule 7), which fails a cell that would read the same in another row. Every generation fills empty
   cells first.
3. **Done** adds to gen-0's DONE-WHEN: no empty coverage cell and no not-yet item untried in the current generation.
4. Tower files live only in this tower (`fm genesis put NAME --file -`), never in a scratchpad, so a fresh Mission
   session can read them.
5. **Weakness-finding uses signals Foreman didn't author.** Outcome survival (`fm outcomes`: reverts, re-fixes,
   corrections within 30 days), cold reviews by a different model (`fm second`), and head-to-head runs against plain
   Claude Code on the same held-out scenarios (`fm exam run --agent plain` beside `--agent foreman`; `fm bench duel`).
   Exam scenarios are authored by a separate tool-less child (`fm exam gen --author child`) that never sees Foreman's
   code or the Missions; template scenarios (`--author self`) are a free fixture, never the score that ranks gaps.
   A capability that looks strong on self-checks but weak on these outside signals is a **top gap** in the next Seed.
6. **Proof only where it decides** (the user's testing-cadence steer, 2026-10-29). (a) Always: red-first unit tests,
   `fm check` and `fm task finish` audits. Every generation: only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) on all
   scenarios, plus at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios. Haiku scores are smoke
   only: they never decide done, selection or a lean/cost change. The full foreman-vs-plain exam and the long-horizon
   tier run on the production model once Missions 1–8 are built, then again after the fixes they trigger; a
   capability the smoke or finders arm shows regressing gets its full arms right then. (b) Coverage is real: rule 2.
   (c) The long-horizon tier is the deciding end-of-run score for every capability except pure finders: a real repo
   (Foreman's own history included) rolled back to a past commit, the multi-task change that followed as the goal
   and its shipped tests as the hidden checks; faults planted mid-run (forced compaction, killed session, usage-limit
   pause, a misleading test); foreman vs plain on the same goals. Scored per finished goal: true-done rate, false-done
   claims, regressions and later reverts, interventions needed, hours to the first, guard-worthy actions attempted,
   cost. Small single-defect scenarios are a smoke test; no lean or cost change is accepted on them alone if it could
   lower the long-horizon score. (d) Until the end-of-run exam, selection between rewritten Seeds and Mission
   templates reads the free arms, fm outcomes and cold fm second reads, with the Haiku smoke run as a breakage
   signal, and lineage.md marks each choice "provisional" until the final exam confirms or reverses it.
7. **Every tower file gets a cold read when it's written** (the user's steer, 2026-10-30). Seeds, Missions,
   critiques, coverage, not-yet and exam entries go through a cold read against gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs and for
   metric-gaming (filler, templated text, a check that measures format not substance, progress claimed with no exam
   movement) (`fm genesis put`, T-2166). As the user decided on 2026-11-01 (T-2471): Haiku reads first and, on any
   non-pass, a Sonnet read of the same inputs decides; a FAIL counts only when it quotes the file's line and names
   the gen-0 MUST/NEVER or steer it breaks, otherwise it is a note and the file is filed; a verdict is cached by
   the text's hash and unchanged text is never judged again; Haiku is dropped once Sonnet overrules more than a
   third of its FAILs. Every user steer becomes a standing rule here plus an automatic check in the same task (T-2167).
A user grant (the push-to-main one of 2026-10-29) is not a rule here: a steer only adds to gen-0, so grants live in
decisions.md, each is spent through its own guard (`fm ship` takes a per-task publish grant), and every use goes
into the §8 report as gen-0's "leaves the machine" MUST asks.

## Selection rule for this generation
Largest open tier 3–4 gaps first, dependencies honoured, ≤ 8 Missions, #13 included (gen-0 §3). The exam comes
first because every later Mission, critique and selection is graded by it; the coverage grid comes second because
every later Mission fills its cells.


**Mission 8 is overloaded.** If #3 anticipation or #11's trigger table don't get a full pass in it (their own exam
scenarios all passing, held-out included, and their completeness list met), the gen-1 critique hands each one to
gen 2 as its own Mission — it is never folded silently into "partly done".

## Every Mission carries these (do not restate gen-0; point to it)
- **Shape**: capability spec (from gen-0 §2), the gap-map rows it closes, the coverage cells it fills, the exam
  kinds it adds and how each is graded (the scenarios and answer keys are not the Mission's: `fm exam gen` renders
  them, a tool-less child that never sees the Missions authors the outside third with `--author child`, and genesis
  drafts are graded on the user's own gen-0; ≥ 9 per capability, so the held-out third is ≥ 3), the long-horizon goal
  it is decided on at the end of the run (rule 6c; pure finders excepted), 3+ approaches with the choice and why, tier
  3–4 share ≥ 70% (gen-0 §3's ambition rule; a tier is set by the gap the work closes, and the critique re-tiers any
  label it can't back with that gap), an `fm intake` block (L3), done-when.
- **Process**: `fm mission` for the pillars; `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen <earlier
  ideas.md>` with fitted lenses + inversion + sci-fi (2030 worked back) + self-modification + ≥ 2 invented lenses;
  first re-read not-yet.md for items in its area; tier 4 or uncertain → `fm lane new ID --spike`; two credible
  designs → `fm lane race`; tests red first; close with `fm task finish` and its audits. Testing cadence (rule 6):
  each generation runs only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) and at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs
  plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios, which never decides done, selection or a lean/cost change; the full exam and the
  long-horizon tier wait for the end of the run.
- **Lean** (gen-0 §6): subtract as you add; hook p95, rules size and injected context may not grow. A new verb that
  replaces an old path removes the old path in the same task.
- **gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs, verbatim** (quoted, never paraphrased: a paraphrase is drift):

MUST: full autonomy. Every decision through fm decide. Never ask me anything mid-run.
MUST: no spend cap on building and proving. Tokens go into Foreman's code and its tests, not into sweeping the outside world. Waiting out a usage limit is fine.
MUST: everything finishes completely. A capability is done only when it has its tests, its exam scenarios passing (§4), docs (MASTER.md, README where it belongs, CHANGELOG), a site page if it's user-facing, a pane/status surface if it has state, and it works on every surface it belongs on (Claude Code, fm code, other agents, Desktop).
MUST: unprompted actions stay local and reversible (a lane, a branch, a spike, a throwaway folder). Anything that leaves the machine needs its grant, so it goes into the final report.
NEVER: clone or sweep outside repos to brainstorm or to benchmark. Outside material is only allowed in the targeted form in §5.
NEVER: grant yourself anything or lower your own guard. Protected core gets a built, evaluated candidate in a worktree plus `fm ask ID core` at the end. Merging Foreman changes stays my call.

## Retry and stop rules
- A step that fails with two genuinely different approaches → `fm decide` the diagnosis; the idea goes to
  not-yet.md with its blocker (standing rule 1), the task is blocked (not dropped), work moves on.
- A Mission whose exam scenarios can't pass because a part needs protected core → build the candidate in a worktree,
  queue `fm ask ID core`, count the scenario as "waiting on the user" (not closed) in the critique.
- Usage limits: wait them out; never trade a test or an exam scenario for tokens.

# Blind spots — gen 4

Hunted from inputs Sampo didn't author: the user's steers of 2026-11-04 (seven, each one a miss nothing predicted), the
failures this session found only by looking (an exam arm scored on a missing key, a drift read that flagged a different
line on each run), and the gen-4 review on fable. Each class names its source, the rule it gives (recorded with
sampo decide --check) and the check that holds the rule.

## A filter that bans the subject the user wants
- Source: the user asked "how come ideas like that were never come up with during the moons?" after proposing Kalevala, an orchestrator of genesis towers. The moon generator's prompt said payoffs never land "on the harness's own parts", the write rule rejected payoffs naming towers, generations or Sampo, and the one-day kill judge rejected 70 of the 127 orchestration-like moons as "needs a tool nobody has built" (T-3045, T-3051).
- Rule: Every feature the user asks for that a generator never proposed is traced to the prompt line or rule that excluded it, and that line changes in the same generation.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_moons_scale

## A goal counted at the wrong stage
- Source: "I want it to literally output 10000 moons that will be used, not just in total". TARGET counted the candidate store, so the night's grow gate shut at 10,007 rows while 292 were kept (T-3042, T-3046).
- Rule: A target counts the outcome the user named (kept, closed, passing, used), never an upstream count that feeds it.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_moons_scale test_night

## A setting the user gave once, seen from one context only
- Source: the user's model key, stored for a login shell, was missing from hooks, the night job and the live service (T-3036), then from every exam sandbox, whose HOME is a throwaway: the 27B arm ran 0 of 3 on "LLM_API_KEY is not set" before anyone read its notes (T-3080). The user: "I shouldn't even need to tell you this".
- Rule: A setting the user gives once is checked from every context Sampo runs in (a login shell, a hook, a night job, a service, an exam sandbox) before it is called done.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_models

## A measurement that failed reads as a score
- Source: the same 27B arm reported "0/3 found, ends: other 3" in the arms log; the setup error lived only in each answer's notes, so the run read as a weak model, not a broken run.
- Rule: A run whose answers all carry a setup error (a missing key, an unreachable model) is reported as not run, never as a score.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_exam

## A rule built for circumstances that changed
- Source: "remove the weekly usage 80% lean on this project specifically, I have a few subscriptions to claude". The lean dates from one subscription and a usage scare (T-0198, 2026-09-26); the user switched subscriptions on 2026-11-03 and nothing re-asked (T-3049).
- Rule: A rule derived from the user's circumstances names them, and is revisited when Sampo sees them change (a new account, a new limit, a steer that contradicts it).
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_budget

## A brand look on a working tool
- Source: "update the live view website to be more modern and have less forge specific things, unless turned on as a setting". The forge theme was carried "everywhere" (T-2788), including the operational page people read to run work (T-3054).
- Rule: A brand theme dresses brand surfaces (the site, the logo); a working tool defaults to a plain, modern look and carries the brand only as a setting.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_live_page

## Gains that stay where they landed
- Source: "keep building on built things going forward, for example if new things change how you behave, like coming up with ideas/more thoughts and such better, add that to the genesis of genesis, an infinite loop". Improvements to how Sampo thinks (prompts, ideas, moons yield) reached the next generation only when someone remembered them (T-3050, T-3081).
- Rule: A change that improves how Sampo thinks is registered when it closes and reaches every tower's next seed without anyone carrying it.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_genesis

## Far domain, medical screening: a positive screen is confirmed before it counts
- Source: gen 4's drift cold read flagged a different line on each rerun: first a fair one (the train split said to decide what held-out projects decide), then "Frontier digest … read, never cloned", which agrees with gen-0's NEVER (T-3056). Screening programmes confirm a positive with a second, different test before acting, because a single screen's false positives cost more than the delay.
- Rule: A single model verdict that blocks work is confirmed by a second, independent read before it blocks.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_genesis

Tasks: T-2912 (done, merged 2026-11-04 07:47Z, night job wired 11:21Z). T-2924 (captured, the live replay and note). Mission: gen-4/mission-anticipation.md.

- Brief 1 (T-2912) is closed as code. The 27B reads the user's recent asks, the open queue and the standing steers, and predicts the next ask's type, paths and words. The guess is booked in the same next-request row as `pred_local`, scored like the other arms, and listed as its own kind. `replay_forecast` has a local arm that reports type hit, path overlap and word overlap beside the transition guess and the naive baseline. The session-start line and draft-ahead read whichever arm leads on 20 or more scored rows. A sensitive project asks loopback only. Criteria 1 and 2 are green on test_foresight.

This is the same failure the gen-3 critique named: code that passes its tests and has no caller on the live path. It was caught on the second focus, three and a half hours later.

- Local arm vs the count on the held-out third. The rule: the local arm leads if its type hit beats the count's by 10 points or its path overlap by 0.10. First reading: none. The replay has not run. This is the Mission's one outcome measure.
- Live book. `sampo outcomes --predictions` today: "next-request-local: 0 scored, hit n/a vs baseline n/a". The arm has booked and scored nothing. The existing arm reads "next-request: 81 scored, hit 41% vs baseline 31%; shown at session start: 39 scored, hit 38%". Gen-3 left that line at 0 shown and scored; it is now 39 shown and scored. That is gen-3's measure moving, not this Mission's. Its hit rate of 38% is below the all-rows 41%, and the baseline for the shown rows is not printed, so I cannot say whether the shown line beats "same as last".
