# Critique — Mission 7, getting the tools it lacks (gen 4, #5)

Tasks: T-2917 (done, merged 2026-11-04 08:38Z). T-2932 (captured, the live batch and bench rows; depends on T-2949). T-2949 (captured, a FIX for the audit's findings). T-2878 step 4 (planned). Mission: gen-4/mission-getting-the-tools-it-lacks.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1 (T-2917) is closed as code. `sampo playbooks eval NAME --real --model PROFILE` answers each brief through an own or loopback profile, never `claude -p`, and books the profile in playbook-evals.jsonl. `sampo playbooks small NAME --model PROFILE` drafts a variant on the local writer and drafts held-out briefs from the original when it has none. It keeps the variant only when its lift is at least the original's. `playbooks show NAME --model PROFILE` serves the kept variant, the coverage line counts variants, and Smith's phase prompt for a local profile carries the variant routed for the task's type, cut to the profile's context. It reuses `sampo.smallcards` (T-2909) and the existing eval. No second store.
- Criteria 1 to 3 and 5 are ticked on tests (test_playbook_evals, test_code). Two live criteria were cut away at 08:23Z and moved to T-2932: criterion 4 (a first batch on the 27B and one small GPU model, with a lift table) and the bench rows for `sampo code bench` with and without a variant. The reason in the log: the endpoint grows moons and the GPU runs the exam. T-2932 is captured and now depends on T-2949.
- Review found a real defect and the task did not fix it. T-2949 says `smallcards._variant_prompt` hands the writer the exact "has" phrases the eval briefs check, then scores the variant on those briefs. A variant can pass by containing the phrases. The task's own lesson says "never score a generated artefact on checks its writer was shown: hold the eval briefs out of the writer's prompt". The lesson exists and the code in the merge still breaks it, so the keep rule is partly circular. The Mission's Risks section promised "briefs drafted from the original before the variant, held by a test". The order is held; the leakage of check phrases is not.

## Measures (first readings and due dates)
- Lift table per playbook and profile (kept, refused, mean lift gained). First reading: none. `state/playbook-evals.jsonl` still has 2 rows, both from 2026-10-22 on the scripted "literal" model. There is no research note small-playbooks. Not one real model has been measured against one playbook. Due: T-2932, after T-2949; no date set.
- Corpus size. Zero kept variants on this machine, as far as the ledger and eval file show. The user's standing ask is "thousands of skills and playbooks written for smaller models". The tooling for that now exists and the count is 0.
- Smith bench with and without a variant. First reading: none. `state/code-bench.jsonl` has 13 rows; none is a with-variant row.
- Taxonomy, from the same T-2878 work, since small models are the target. On 15 local runs, 40% ended out of steps, 20% had a plan refused by the plan gate (T-3016 now returns the refusal to the planner once; T-3016 is planned, not merged), 7% hit the reasoning budget, 7% timed out. `sampo exam taxonomy s5-019` for gemma 12B reads one scenario ending on budget. T-3006's reasoning arms on s5-019 with gemma 12B read off 0/3 fixed, state 1/3 fixed. That is a smoke signal, n of 3. The 27B arms need an API key this session does not store. These say where small models fail: running out of steps and plan refusal, not following a playbook's wording. A variant that lifts brief-following will not touch the top failure.
- Friction lead from the Mission: sessions reached for `fm models`, `fm andon` and `fm shot` by name. No alias or capture is recorded as made; I did not check further.

## What failed
- The Mission is the one most about measured help, and its measured part is the part that did not run. The tool for lift exists; no lift exists.
- The keep rule is circular as merged (T-2949). Until it is fixed, any batch run would produce lifts that overstate the variants. Running T-2932 first would waste the endpoint's slot.
- The grounding said small models "can do the work" (4B and e4b closed 4 of 5 seeds; the 27B closed 1 of 5, its misses endpoint errors). That is a seed count of 5, a smoke signal, and the Mission built on it as fact.

That was a fair cut. But gen-0 #5's other half (find, build, test and use a tool; queue install grants) has no brief at all in gen-4.

- Run T-2949 before T-2932, in that order, and put the order in T-2932's criteria. Score variants on briefs the writer never saw.
- Pick the playbooks by the failure taxonomy. Cards for "stay within the step budget" and "revise the plan after a refusal" go first. The 40% and 20% buckets are where a card could change a close.
- Set a date for the first lift table and run it on a free slot, with the GPU profile as the one that is free by default.

Tasks: T-2913 (done, merged 2026-11-04 07:27Z, closed 07:59Z). Mission: gen-4/mission-goal-to-finish.md.

The evidence line for it is `sampo goal plan` exiting 0, and its output was a note about an unrelated task ("T-1234 was fixed later by T-1235"). - Live plan. `sampo goal plan` today lists the 13 capabilities of gen-0 §2 ("Initiative" through "Genesis as a feature"), the three DONE-WHEN clauses, and the standard items, with no duplicate "works on the web UI surface" lines. The plan lists items but nothing applied them. The Mission's stated purpose was that "the live Genesis goal can tell done from stopped". It cannot yet. The final step, `goal plan --apply` on the live mandate, was never run, or was run and not kept. This is the biggest finding.

But the criterion that would have checked "the verdict names the unmet items on this project" was worded as a plan listing, so it passed without it.
- False-done class. The Mission's long-horizon goal: on a replayed long goal pointing at a spec file, the done claim is refused while an entry is unmet, and the "planned but not built" class falls (9 of 31 failed checks over 12 goals in research/long-false-done.md). No replay has run. `sampo genesis status` still shows long-horizon "behind on 6 same goal(s): foreman 0/6 done, checks 4/20, false-done 6" against plain 1/6 done, false-done 5. I did not find a number that moved. Due: the next long-horizon run, which needs a replay that points at a spec file.
- Gen-3's goal-to-finish measures: the gen-3 critique is stored; this Mission did not carry any of them back, and none is named in its file.

## What failed
- A green plan is not a working goal. The criteria tested the reader (parse the doc, dedupe, map checks) and not the thing the user cares about, that the live goal gives a verdict with named misses. The same lesson as gen-3's anticipation critique: tests on synthetic goals prove the logic, the premise needs a reading on live state, and here the live reading was weaker than the claim.
- Proposals the planner still emits are junk. The plan prints "`fm` verbs that create, start, and stop goals (names not yet verified in the repo)" and similar. They are marked "not added", so they do no harm, but they name the old `fm` and verbs that do not exist. The Mission's grounding named this problem ("proposals naming verbs that don't exist") and the model line filter still lets it through as a proposal.
- Every item is a user item with no check except three. The brief said so itself ("leave the other items to their linked tasks"). Today 13 capability items have no link to a task, so even after apply the verdict would say 13 unmet with no path to done.
- The builder lane worked fast (14 minutes, merged in one pass) and the main thread closed 32 minutes later. Nothing went wrong in the hand-off. The gap was the criterion, not the lane.

## What the next Seed should change
- Run `goal plan --apply` on the live mandate as a first step of the next Mission 3 brief, and record the verdict before and after in the log. If a person must approve the mutation, ask once through `sampo ask` and move on.
- Link each capability item to its exam: item "Exhaustive thinking" checks `sampo exam scorecard` row 2, or the capability's own task. A goal whose items have no checks cannot be done.
- Write criteria on the verdict, not the plan: "on this project, `goal verdict` names N unmet items" with N in the criterion and the command in the verify line.
- Strip proposals that name non-existent verbs or the old `fm` name before printing. They teach the reader to ignore the section.
- Build the replay for "done claim refused while a spec entry is unmet". It is the only reading that tests whether the false-done class falls, and no replay exists.

# Critique — Mission 8, moonshot (gen 4, #8)

Tasks: T-2918 (done; its live run split out to T-2954, captured). Mission: gen-4/mission-moonshot.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1, part one: the M-02 slice. T-2918 is closed and merged. `sampo moons regen PATH` (regen.py) deletes one
  module in a throwaway worktree. It asks the model for the module back from its intent only: the briefs that name
  it, its map entry, its tests and the names its importers use. It runs the module's own tests and prints each result.
  Review added safeguards the first build lacked: an isolated test environment, a symlink-safe delete, and "a down
  model moves on". A reply that imports outside the original imports, or does not compile, is refused unrun. It
  lands nothing.
- Brief 1, part one, the run: not done. The Mission's whole point was a result: "2 or more modules round-trip" earns
  "Advanced: M-02 slice". T-2918's third criterion was rewritten mid-close to "the slice run is split out", and the
  result file bench/moonshot/m02-slice-result.json reads `"ran": false`. Its note says the GPU and the remote endpoint
  were busy. The Mission file's own rule said the Advanced line is written only when the slice result is filed. So
  there is no Advanced line, and the floor (advance one extreme or massive moon by a stage) is unmet for gen 4.
  `sampo moons status` still shows M-02 at the kill stage and "0 built".
- Brief 1, part two: the ecology moons. Filed. The catalogue went from 58 to 61 of 100 (xhigh 4 to 5, massive 19 to
  21), and the closing criterion, `sampo moons check` after `rate`, was met. I did not re-read the new blocks for
  wildness. The reviewer's wild score on them is the only judge, and I have not read it.
- Closing a task by moving its hard criterion to a new task is legal under the rules. It is also how an outcome
  slides one generation. Here it moved because the endpoint was busy at 08:10 and the 10k funnel was using it.

## Measures (first readings and due dates)
- Slice round-trip count. Planned measure: modules that regrow and pass every original test, on the 27B first and
  Haiku second. First reading: none. 0 of the 20 sampled leaf modules have been run. Due: when T-2954 runs. It is
  captured, not started.
- Catalogue size, which the Mission shares with self-triggering. Before: 58 moons. Today: 61 moons, and the
  candidates store stands at 10,007 (292 survivors in 280 families), closed by T-2865 in this session by hand.
- Kill-tested extreme or massive moons: 1 of 20 (gen-4 opened at 1 of 18). That means the climb the Mission cited
  (M-18, then kills for M-21 to M-28) did not move. This Mission did not claim it would.

## Outside signals
- None from a user. The Mission's premise, that the user would ask for exactly this step, came from the prediction.
  No steer has confirmed or denied it in the days since. It is not scored here.

## What failed
- The headline did not run. The code that could prove M-02 now exists, and no reading says whether a Sampo module
  can be regrown from its briefs. This is the third time a moon advanced as machinery rather than as a result
  (gen-3 had the kill script, gen-4 has the slice runner). Building the runner is easy to close. The run is the
  claim.
- The failure was foreseeable. Grounding noted the 27B closed 1 of 5 seeds on endpoint errors, and still planned the
  run inside the same close as the build. A run that needs the one scarce GPU should have been its own first task,
  ordered before the build that did not need the GPU.
- The ecology moons were filed in the same close with no stated reading of how wild they are. The measure for a moon
  is its wild score, and the critique cannot quote one.

## What the next Seed should change
- Make T-2954 gen-5's first task, and give it a rule: it holds the GPU lock before any other local job starts, and
  the night's $0 jobs yield to it. Then record the true count, with the failures. A result of 0 of 20 is a finding
  about how well briefs pin code. It is not a reason to drop the moon.
- A Mission whose floor is "advance a stage" gets one criterion that reads the stage in `sampo moons status` after
  the close. No split-out may carry that criterion.
- Count the stage movement in the critique from the catalogue, never from the task title.

# Critique — Mission 6, self-triggering (gen 4, #11)

Tasks: T-2916 (done). Mission: gen-4/mission-self-triggering.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1 (T-2916) is closed and merged, with a second commit from review. `night.jobs` lists a `moons grow` job (calls
  capped per night) and a `moons funnel` job at zero dollars. It lists them only when an own or loopback model answers,
  the project is not sensitive, and the store is under its 10,000 target. Both take `--local-only`: a call the local
  model cannot answer stops the run with its reason and never falls back to Haiku. Review made the funnel job list
  whenever rows wait to be funnelled, and made the local-only rule hold for every call, not only the first. It is the
  Mission's whole scope, as planned. No new verb, unit or hook.
- All three criteria are ticked. The third was `sampo night --dry-run` listing both jobs at $0.00. The task log
  records the reading at close. I could not re-read it today, for the reason below.

## Measures (first readings and due dates)
- Outcome measure: the catalogue's size after a real night, with the two Moons features costing $0 that night.
  First reading: none. No night has run since the jobs landed (the timer fires at 02:30, and the jobs closed at about
  10:38 UTC on 2026-11-04). The Mission's own done-when says "one real night has run both jobs". That is not met.
  Due: the first night after this critique, then a week.
- Live reading today: `sampo night --dry-run` plans 11 jobs, about $1.98 of $2.00. Eight are $0 chores (scout, dream,
  cold files, guard cases, steer checks, compost, consolidate, sentinel), plus a new "next request" job at $0. The
  paid ones are research debt (about $0.45) and court (about $1.53). The queue is skipped as over the limit. The two
  Moons jobs are not on the list.
- Why not: the candidates store is 10,007, over the 10,000 target. T-2865 closed this very session and grew the store
  by hand. So the gate did what it was built to do. That also means the first real night will probably run no Moons
  job at all. This is my reading of the gate, not a run. The measure as written cannot move until the target is raised
  or the funnel has rows waiting.
- Other shifts today: the 02:30 timer's last run is not in the ledger as a `night` event that I can see. `sampo triggers`
  shows the `night` trigger fired once in total. The schedule exists and little rides it.

## Outside signals
- None. The only new input is that the live page (T-2997 to T-3027) now steers sessions, but it does not start work
  by itself. It is steering from a user who is present, not a trigger.

## What failed
- The Mission solved yesterday's gap. When it was written the store stood at 4,879 of 10,000. By the time it closed,
  one interactive burst (T-2865) had reached 10,007, so the feature it shipped is switched off by its own gate. The
  feature is correct. It was sized to a number that moved under it, and nobody re-read the store between plan and close.
- The measure needs a night, so the exam cannot be run in the generation that builds it. This is the third Mission
  where the outcome waits on a clock (anticipation, gen 3, was the same). The Mission said "read after a night has
  run" and still ticked done-when in the plan. The critique can only say planned, not moved.
- The Mission left the paid half of the night alone. Court at $1.53 of a $2.00 limit still eats most of the money, and
  the queue is skipped every night for lack of it. That is the actual constraint on what starts without the user.

## What the next Seed should change
- Raise the target as part of the Mission, or write the gate as "rows waiting" so it does not turn off at a number. A
  store that stops growing should stop by evidence of diminishing novelty, not by a constant.
- Give the night a second kind of $0 work. Candidates that do not need a catalogue: T-2910's local brainstorm for the
  next Mission, the model bench rerun (T-2886), a graded morning card. The morning card is what lets the critique read
  what ran and why it stopped.
- A Mission that depends on a night reads its first real night in its own critique, or says plainly the critique is
  early. Gen 5's critique of this Mission should quote the ledger event for the first night, whichever jobs ran.

# Critique — Mission 5, staying lean and safe (gen 4, #12)

Tasks: T-2915 (done). Mission: gen-4/mission-staying-lean-and-safe.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1 (T-2915) is closed and merged, with a follow-up merge for the fmregen bullet. MASTER.md is now an index.
  The File map and Operations bodies moved into seven shards under docs/map (files-1, files-lib-1 to -3, ops-1 to -3).
  MASTER.md keeps one index line per entry with its link. Every other section stayed whole.
- A helper, `core.master_text`, reads MASTER.md and the shards together. Doctor's self-docs and file-map checks,
  the close-time file-map row check, release-check's runnable fences, and the scout and regen readers use it. Nothing
  that read the map lost a line. A test holds a word-multiset comparison: the moved text is the same text, reflowed.
- All four criteria are ticked. A test holds the three size limits: MASTER.md at most 90,000 bytes, each shard at
  most 90,000, and no line over 2,000 characters.
- Planned but not done: the Mission's two side leads. The `sampo burden` reading (77 characters a turn on the working
  copy against 40 on released versions) and the 2.9 GB of exam state went to "Hands to the next generation", as
  planned. They were not touched.

## Measures (first readings and due dates)
- Size. Before: 462,922 bytes, 779 lines, about 115,000 tokens, with 53 lines over 2,000 characters. Today I read
  `wc -c MASTER.md`: 82,232 bytes. `awk 'length>2000'` finds 0 long lines. Shards total 435,840 bytes. The largest
  is 76,047. These are readings of the files, not of a Read call. Moved, as the criteria define.
- Read failures. Before: in the events window, Read on MASTER.md failed 7 times and worked once, while 83 Bash calls
  grepped or sed-cut it (83 of 91 lookups). Planned reading: those two counts after the close, from state/events.jsonl.
  First reading: I have not re-counted them, and the close was only hours ago. Due 2026-11-11, on a week of sessions.
- Orientation in two reads. The Mission's long-horizon goal is a fresh agent that orients in two reads. No fresh-agent
  run has been done. Planned, not measured.
- Doctor stays green with the new reader. The full gate passed at close. That is the safety half of "lean and safe".

## Outside signals
- None. The complaint came from the gen-3 cross-cutting review, which was a Sampo reviewer's, not a user's.

## What failed
- The first claim of "lean" was a size, and size was the right thing to move. But the sum went up. Sections still
  total 435,840 bytes of shards plus 82,232 of index, 518,072 bytes, against 462,922 before. The index lines add
  weight and the text did not shrink. A session that wants one module's entry now reads two files, where it used to
  grep one. The Mission trades a refused Read for an extra hop. Whether that is a win is the open measure, not a fact.
- The rest of the dimension was untouched. The model-facing cost of the map is its size only if sessions read it. The
  83 Bash lookups suggest they grep it, so a cheaper index may change little.
- The shards are alphabetical by module, not by what a task needs. Each of three lib shards runs 65,000 to 76,000
  bytes, still more than 16,000 tokens, so one Read of a shard is still heavy.
- One plan weakness. The Mission's exam was "a read of MASTER.md succeeds", which is a unit test. The harness used
  was `bash` on a file, not the Read tool a model uses with a line cap. I cannot say a real Read succeeds on this
  file without running one, and I was told not to run things here.

## What the next Seed should change
- Count what a lookup costs end to end: tokens spent to get one module's entry, before and after, on ten real lookups
  taken from the events log. That is the true measure, not the file size.
- Add a verb-less pointer: have the global rules say "start with MASTER.md's index, then one shard". The rules line
  written by setup.py:36 still just says "System map".
- Pick up the two held leads as one small Mission: the `sampo burden` 77 against 40 difference, and the 3.2 GB of
  project state (2.9 GB in exam/). Pruning exam state touches the held-out runs, so it needs its own ask.
- Re-read the 14 test files that read MASTER.md for any that now pass vacuously, because they look in the index
  and the line they want is in a shard.

# Critique — Mission 3, verifying anything (gen 4, #6)

Tasks: T-2914 (done). Mission: gen-4/mission-verifying-anything.md.

## Closed vs planned
- Brief 1 (T-2914) is closed and merged. Two things landed.
  - Plan time: for a user's M or L brief not yet started, `plan_gaps` (core.py) names each clause of the Raw request
    that no criterion checks, with the `sampo task ac add` line that would close it. It uses a new
    `recall.unchecked_clauses`, because `recall.bind` marks every clause "no green run" before anything has run. A
    clause echoed in Non-goals counts as accounted. S tasks, harness and hook plans and Sampo-sourced briefs are not
    gated.
  - Rollup: the meaning kind now splits into the user's words and Sampo's own notes. The task log records the live
    split: meaning-user 244 and meaning-notes 355, summing to 599, which equals the old meaning count. The sum is held
    by a test, so the split cannot quietly shrink.
- Review changed the plan gate after the builder shipped it. It now skips title restatements and batch hosts, and
  four test fixtures had to be rewritten to echo their request in a criterion (test_recall, test_second,
  test_judgment). That is a cost the Mission's risks did not list: the gate broke tests that had passed for months.
- Left out, as planned: three-valued verdicts, and a local model that drafts checks. The latter waits on the
  vacuous-check proof (T-2878).

## Measures (first readings and due dates)
- Share of user M and L closes landing with meaning unproven. Before: 53 of 302. After: not recomputed. The task log
  says so itself: "user M/L share not recomputed (53 of 302 per the brief)". Planned reading: closes after T-2914,
  read at the end of the window. There are no such closes yet worth a share, because the gate began mid-day.
  Due 2026-11-11, and again 2026-12-04 (30 days).
- The rollup split. First reading at close: 244 user, 355 notes. Today the whole rollup reads "unproven: 809 (done
  in the last 30 days)". The 809 is the sum of all kinds (typed 37, red 75, ui-unshot 22, tui-unshot 8, docs 108,
  and others). The meaning part is not the whole of it, and I could not re-split meaning today without running a
  long query. So no movement is claimed. The first look at the rows suggests many of the listed meaning rows are
  provenance lines such as "(noticed by an agent;", which is exactly what the notes half exists to hold.
- Honest reading of the split: 355 of 599 meaning rows, 59%, are Sampo's own words, not the user's. That is a real
  finding. More than half of "meaning unproven" was never the user's. The old number overstated how much the user
  had been left unchecked, by about half. It also means the user's count, 244, is the one that must go to zero.

## Outside signals
- None. This Mission's evidence is all Sampo's own rollup. The one thing a user has done in the same days is steer the
  live page. That gives no read on whether plan-time gaps help.

## What failed
- Nothing is proven to be better, only more honestly counted. The gate asks for a check per clause. It cannot
  tell if the check is real. The Mission's own risk said bind's two-shared-words rule could pass a clause against an
  unrelated criterion. There is no number for how often that happens.
- The measure waited on closes that do not yet exist, and the builder did not take the "before" reading's other half.
  So the critique has the denominator before and nothing after. The fix was one command, `sampo prove --rollup`
  filtered to user M and L, run on a stated date.
- The rollup keeps growing. 809 unproven in 30 days is large, and kinds like red (75), docs (108) and the unshot UI rows remain. The Mission aimed at one kind of the gap. It
  moved the label of the biggest kind and did not close one row.
- Rival plan reading: its likeliest was a plan-schema field. The builder chose a gap in the existing gate. That was
  the cheaper path and is right. The risk it carries is that the gap lives in core.py's plan checks, not in a field
  a later tool can read.

## What the next Seed should change
- Close the 244 by proof, with a sweep: for each user-words row, either add a criterion that can fail or file the
  clause in Non-goals. Rank by recency. A Mission that works that list is measurable the same day.
- Take the after reading with a command, on a named date, in the task log: user M and L closes after T-2914, how
  many carry meaning-unproven. The Mission wrote the want and left the number out.
- Fix the 59%: the provenance lines ("noticed by an agent", "Captured by fm check") should never enter Raw request.
  That is #7's capture-format question, and it stops 355 false rows at the source.
- Then do the three-valued verdict (proved, unproven, disproved) as the next step the Mission itself named.

# Mission 2 — anticipation (gen 4, #3): a guess that reads the user's words

Task: T-2912 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-4/seed.md row 2 → gen-0.md #3: "Anticipation. A model of me, my projects and my machines (requests,
corrections, habits, what breaks). It predicts the next request and drafts it on spec in a lane, and flags problems
before they happen (grow `fmforesight`)." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here
unchanged.

## Capability
The prediction is the root of #3: the session-start line, draft-ahead and the user model all hang off it. Today the
guess is a count of type transitions plus the paths of the last ask of that type. It reads no words. The live book
(predictions.jsonl, read 2026-11-04) holds 57 scored guesses: 25 type hits against the naive baseline's 21 (44% vs
37%), path overlap 0.172 against 0.166. Draft-ahead, which runs only while the guess beats the baseline, has drafted
once and been adopted never. This Mission gives the guess a second arm that reads what a person would read: the
user's recent asks in their own words, the open queue and the standing steers. It runs on the local 27B at no cost,
and it is shown only after a held-out replay says it leads.

## Grounding (each read in the code on 2026-11-04)
- plugin/lib/sampo/foresight.py:332 `predict(reqs)`: the type from transitions out of the last type, the paths from
  the newest ask of that type. T-2449's note in its docstring: changing what it reads made it trail the baseline.
- foresight.py:347 `prediction_tick` books one next-request row per user ask ({pred, base}) and scores the pending one
  with `type_hit`, `base_type_hit`, `overlap` and `base_overlap`. It is called from the hourly tick at
  plugin/lib/sampo/night.py:389 (the timer foreman-tick-foreman-4a056f is installed and fired at 00:00).
- foresight.py:388 `prediction_kinds` scores each kind against its baseline and mutes one that trails it over
  `MUTE_MIN` (foresight.py:267, 20) rows. foresight.py:245 `_next_line` shows a guess only while its kind leads.
  plugin/lib/sampo/draft.py:154 (`ahead`) drafts only on the same condition.
- plugin/lib/sampo/louhi.py:781 `replay_forecast` replays the user's own stream with the last third held out (the
  exam's foresight arm calls it at louhi.py:3537). This is the zero-token harness the new arm joins.
- Callers of the shared read, found by grep (the calibrated-judgment critique's rule): `foresight._requests` is read
  by louhi.py:787, draft.py:163 and foresight.py itself; `prediction_kinds` by outcomes.py:200 and :207,
  triggers.py:285 and draft.py:154. The new kind is added beside next-request, so none of them changes meaning.
- The surface is in use (the anticipation critique's rule): 60 next-request rows and 24 `shown` rows in the book; the
  session-start line printed "next-request predictions 44% vs baseline 37%" in `sampo triggers` today.
- The local model: models.json `jarvis` (qwen3.8-27b, own, 2 slots), routed by plugin/lib/sampo/moonscale.py:379
  `_local`, the same rule T-2910 reuses.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #3)
- understand × fm code: the user model reads the asks' words, not only their types.
- plan × headless/server: the guess is made on the tick with no cloud call and no session open.

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
fm mission, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 (research/brainstorm-20261104-002824:
366 distinct ideas; its --deepen rounds were dropped by today's risk budget, recorded with sampo decide). Grounded:
- "Settle predictions by text similarity" (round 1) and the cross-bred "Close the prediction loop with edits,
  pushbacks and text-similarity settling": partial. Score rows hold type and path overlap only. Brief 1 adds a word
  overlap for the arm that predicts words. Its kill test ("agreement under 80% with a hand-judged 20") needs a hand
  judge; the replay's type and path numbers decide instead.
- "Draft the predicted ask speculatively and verify it cheaply": built near T-2407 (draft-ahead). Its kill test
  ("count accepted drafts; if under 3, the spend is waste") already reads 0 of 1. The draft waits on a better guess,
  which is brief 1.
- "Wild: Hold a nightly ghost user that predicts a handful of asks and is scored by the morning": new. It builds on
  brief 1's arm and goes to the next #3 Mission if the replay shows the arm leads.
- "Escalate to frontier only when local models disagree": new, held for T-2878's control step.

## Approaches
1. A local predictor beside `predict`, booked as `pred_local` in the same row, scored the same way plus a word
   overlap, listed as its own kind, replayed on the same held-out third. Likely outcome: a guess that knows what the
   user is in the middle of. Fails if: it doesn't beat the count on held-out rows; it then stays in shadow.
2. use what exists: tune `predict()`. Fails if: T-2449 found tuning made it trail; a count can't read words.
3. do less: settle by word similarity only. Fails if: the guess stays at 44% and draft-ahead stays idle.
4. A 4B decision model for the type. Fails if: the type is the weakest half; paths and words need context.

Choice: 1 (60%). The doubt is that the user's asks come from new ideas history can't predict. The replay measures it.

## Exam (an outcome measure, with a live reading)
- Outcome measure: `replay_forecast` on this project's own stream, held-out third, zero cloud tokens. The local arm
  leads if its type hit beats the count's by 10 points or more, or its path overlap by 0.10 or more. A lead earns the
  session-start line and draft-ahead. Anything less keeps it in shadow, with the numbers filed in
  research/next-request-local. The rule for a windowed signal holds: a guess counts only once the ask after it exists.
- Live reading before close: the book's next scored rows carry `local_type_hit`, and `sampo triggers` prints both arms.
- Exam kinds: #3's forecast scenarios are unchanged; the end-of-run exam reads the replay's new fields.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
The user opens a session and the first line names the ask they were about to type, often enough that a drafted plan
for it is adopted.

## Risks
- Leakage: the replay must give each guess only the asks before it (`reqs[:i]`), never the held-out ask's own text.
  A test checks that.
- The book's integrity: rows stay write-once; a new field, never a rewritten row.
- Privacy: a sensitive project predicts nothing (the existing rule), and the local prompt goes to own or loopback
  profiles only.
- Load: one call per user ask on the tick, two slots, a timeout. A down model books nothing and the tick goes on.

## Lean
No new verb, no new hook, no new file. One arm in an existing book.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: the only #3 predictor that reads meaning.

## Hands to the next generation
The replay's numbers per arm. If the local arm leads: the ghost-user night run and word-level drafts. If it doesn't:
the failure classes (wrong type, wrong area, new idea) as cases for T-2878's small-model control step.

## Done when
T-2912's three criteria are green, the research note is filed, and MASTER.md (fmforesight) and CHANGELOG say it.

- "Price the width at intake and reveal readings only on disagreement" (cross-bred) and "Run the Mission at three
  widths and let outcomes pick": partial. `sampo mission` sets lenses and rounds, but width has a price that only a
  local arm takes to zero. Both wait on brief 1's head-to-head: if the local arm holds up, a width dial has nothing to
  charge for.
- "Show the other readings only when two cold readers disagree": built near T-2229 (`fm genesis put` shows a cold
  reader's FAIL quotes). Not taken.
The kill test the brainstorm wrote for the width idea ("ask the user once … if the answer is always no, drop it")
needs the user present; the head-to-head below replaces it with a measurement that doesn't.

## Approaches
1. A `local` model name in `run_child` and `run_children`, routed through `moonscale._local` and `models.complete` in a
   pool sized by the profile's slots, Haiku for any child the local model can't answer, the answering model booked
   per child. Likely outcome: brainstorms at no cost, and a number that decides the default. Fails if: the local
   replies miss the lens format and parse to few ideas (the test plants one; the head-to-head counts parsed ideas).
2. use what exists: call `moonscale._ask` per child. Fails if: it is serial and books spend under the moons feature.
3. do less: keep local volume in `moons grow` only. Fails if: every Mission brainstorm keeps paying for sonnet while
   the local model idles.
4. A separate `ideas-local` verb. Fails if: it splits the brainstorm skill's one entry point and doubles the parser.

Choice: 1 (75%). The doubt is reply format, measured, not assumed.

## Exam (an outcome measure, with a live reading)
- Outcome measure: the head-to-head on one real gen-4 Mission pack (Mission 2's), same lenses, same `--seen` set, one
  round each, local vs sonnet. Per arm: distinct ideas past `--seen`, and a blind cold judge (`sampo second`, arm
  labels removed) marking each of 40 sampled ideas per arm "grounded in this repo and new" or not. The local arm earns
  the default if its judged-good count reaches 80% of sonnet's. Under 50%, it stays opt-in and the gap is the next
  #2 Mission's lead. Filed as research/ideas-local-vs-cloud.
- Live reading before close: one `sampo ideas --model local --rounds 1` on this project, its manifest showing the
  local profile on every child.
- Exam kinds: #2's scenarios are unchanged. Their session arms run at the end-of-run exam (rule 6).

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
On a held-out long goal, the plan's readings and options come from a brainstorm that cost nothing, and the session
that used them closes more checks than one that didn't.

## Risks
- Format drift: the parser drops malformed bullets silently. Mitigation: a planted malformed reply in the test, and
  parsed-per-child counts in the head-to-head.
- GPU contention with `moons grow` and the bench: one pool sized by `slots`, never more children than the profile
  allows.
- Spend booked wrong: local children book $0 under the `ideas` feature, and a Haiku fallback books its real cost.
- Sensitive projects: loopback only, failing closed, never the cloud.

## Lean
No new verb, one model name, one branch in the child runner. No hook change.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: a brainstorm whose width is free changes what "scale the depth to the risk" can afford.

## Hands to the next generation
The head-to-head number. If the local arm holds up: the width dial (rounds and lenses set by risk, at no cost), and
`sampo mission` defaulting to local. If it doesn't: the failure classes the judge found go to T-2878's control step
(Smith's small-model mode) as its first cases.

## Done when
T-2910's three criteria are green, the research note is filed, and MASTER.md (sampo ideas) and CHANGELOG say it.

# Mission 7 — getting the tools it lacks (gen 4, #5): instructions written for small models, kept on lift

Task: T-2917 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-4/seed.md row 7 → gen-0.md #5 (gen-0.md:42, "Getting the tools it lacks": when it hits something it
can't do, it finds an existing plugin, skill or server or builds one, tests it and uses it, and install grants are
queued for the user, never self-granted; the verbs gen-0 names there are read in gen-0 itself, not restated here).
gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
The tool a small model lacks is instructions it can follow. The user's standing steer (2026-11-03, T-2878): make the
local models match frontier results through scaffolding, and build "thousands of skills, playbooks, UI instructions
and designs written for smaller models", grown every generation. Read on this machine before planning:
- `sampo code bench` history (state/code-bench.jsonl, 2026-11-04): the 4B qwen and the e4b gemma each closed 4 of 5
  seeds as Smith workers. The 27B closed 1 of 5, its four misses endpoint errors, not wrong code. Small models can do
  the work. What they lack is measured help.
- The playbook library has 130 playbooks under plugin/skills/playbooks/references and a with-and-without eval that
  says whether a model does what a playbook asks. It has eval briefs for one playbook
  (plugin/evals/playbooks/verify/tdd-workflow.json), and two runs on record, both on the scripted "literal" model
  (state/playbook-evals.jsonl). Nothing has measured a real model against a playbook, small or large.
So the corpus the user asked for has a home and a gate already. It lacks a writer, a small-model path through the
gate, and briefs.

## Grounding (each read in the code on 2026-11-04)
- plugin/lib/sampo/playbooks.py:1351 `real_model` answers every brief through `ideas.run_child`, which is `claude -p`
  (ideas.py:78), so no local profile can be evaluated. playbooks.py:1342 `literal` is the scripted model.
  playbooks.py:1372 `evaluate` returns {n, with, without, lift}. playbooks.py:1397 `ablate` gives each section's share.

- The module docstring (playbooks.py:1-30): `fm playbooks show NAME` is how the skill loads a playbook, with the
  project's overlay after it. That is the place a per-profile variant is served from.
- plugin/lib/sampo/models.py:786 `complete` is the local call; plugin/lib/sampo/moonscale.py:379 `_local` is the
  routing (own or loopback, loopback only when sensitive).
- The session path that will use a kept variant: plugin/lib/sampo/smith.py:824 `phase` builds each step's system
  prompt from `ACT_PROMPT` (smith.py:169) for whatever profile runs it, and loads no playbook today. A `sampo code`
  run on a local profile is where a small model meets Sampo's instructions. plugin/lib/sampo/playbooks.py:609
  `route(stage)` already names the books for a task's type or stage.
- T-2878 (open, L) plans this as its step 4 ("corpus: the card store, grid and coverage, the A/B gate; bulk on the
  local models"). T-2917 is that step's first M, cut to reuse the playbook library instead of a new store.

## Not-yet items in this area (retried, read only)
- jeff, selfjev-4b: the model bench (`sampo exam models show`, run m20261103-223621959) now has them. jeff scores 0.52
  on intake type and 0.235 on tier, against the majority baseline's 0.595 and 0.58. The `orchestrator` row (the path
  they would replace) has n=0, because no held-out task has a shadow row of the orchestrator's own call. Still blocked.
  It unblocks once orchestrator rows exist on held-out tasks, and the bench shows jeff under the baseline anyway.
- d3:4b (a decision model, not a not-yet item) reads 0.73 on intake type against 0.595: the first local arm to beat a
  baseline on Sampo's own work. Carried to the next #8 or model-layer Mission.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #5)
- build × CLI: `sampo playbooks small` builds the instruction a small model lacks and tests it before keeping it.
- learn × headless/server: the corpus grows on the local models with no session and no spend.

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
fm mission, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 (research/brainstorm-20261104-003757: 369
distinct ideas; --deepen dropped by today's risk budget, one grid lens failed in round 2, both recorded). Grounded:
- "Build the Card Foundry: mine failures, write, cold-test, keep only measured lift" (cross-bred) and "Have the 27B
  write cards, and a different small model test them cold": new, and brief 1. The 27B writes, a small GPU model is
  measured, and lift decides.
- "Gate every card on a bare-model exam before it enters the store": partial. `evaluate` already measures with and
  without. Brief 1 runs it on the bare small model.
- "Re-measure cards when the served model changes, and retire the ones that stopped helping": new. It builds on brief
  1's rows, which book the profile, and is held for the next #5 Mission.
- "Wild: A 'dumbest model' floor: find the smallest model that passes each card's task and print it on the card":
  new. It falls out of running the same variant across the 27B and the 4B/9B profiles. Held.
- Friction seen while grounding: sessions reached for `fm models` (this one too), `fm andon` and `fm shot 1440 --full`
  (`sampo friction`, 2026-11-04). These are tools a session lacked by name. Carried as a #5 lead: an unknown verb a
  session reaches for twice becomes an alias or a capture.

## Approaches
1. Small variants through the existing eval: a local `real_model`, a `small` writer that also drafts briefs from the
   original when it has none, keep-on-lift, `show --model`, coverage in the lint. Smith's phase prompt for a local
   profile carries the kept variant routed for the task's type, so every `sampo code` run on a small model uses it.
   Likely outcome: a corpus growing by playbook × model, each card with a lift, read by the runs it was written for. Fails if: the briefs only test what the variant says. The briefs are
   drafted from the original before the variant exists, and a test holds the order.
2. use what exists: `eval --real` on a cloud model. Fails if: it measures nothing about small models and spends usage.
3. do less: the local eval path only. Fails if: the corpus never starts.
4. A separate card store. Fails if: it duplicates the library's lint, index and eval, and nobody reads it.

Choice: 1 (65%).

## Exam (an outcome measure, with a live reading)
- Outcome measure: per playbook and profile, the original's lift and the variant's lift on held-out briefs, for every
  playbook with briefs plus ten more, on the 27B and one small GPU model. Filed as research/small-playbooks. A
  variant counts only when its lift is at least the original's. The note reports how many were kept, how many
  refused and the mean lift gained.
- Live reading at close: `sampo playbooks show <a kept one> --model <profile>` serves the variant, the lint's
  coverage line counts it, and `sampo code bench` on that profile runs with and without the variant in Smith's
  prompt, both rows in the note (five seeds are a smoke signal, never the verdict).
- Which way the measure may differ from real work: brief-following is an upper bound on usefulness. T-2878's Louhi
  smith arm measures real closes later.
- Exam kinds: #5's tool-find, tool-build and tool-grant scenarios are unchanged.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
On a held-out goal worked by a local model through Smith, the small-model playbooks raise its true-done count over
the same model with the originals.

## Risks
- Circular grading: briefs drafted from the original before the variant, held by a test, and a different small model
  measures the 27B's writing.
- Library bloat: variants sit beside originals under the existing lint (title and shingle duplicates, size ceilings),
  and a refused variant is never saved.
- Context limits: the GPU profiles hold 32,768 tokens. A variant must fit with its task, and the writer is told the
  target profile's context.
- Spend: local only. A cloud model name keeps today's budgeted path.

## Lean
No new store and no new verb: a subcommand and a flag on `sampo playbooks`. The reach is real from the first day,
because Smith's local runs read the kept variants (smith.py:824), and `sampo playbooks show` is the skill's own load
path. No hook.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: the first measured scaffold for small models in Sampo's own instructions.

## Hands to the next generation
The first lift table per playbook and model. The next #5 Mission grows the corpus to design and UI cards on the same
gate, retires cards whose lift decays when a model changes, and gives T-2878's Louhi smith arm (step 1) the variants to
measure on real closes.

T-2917's five criteria are green, the research note is filed, and MASTER.md (fmplaybooks) and CHANGELOG say it.

# Mission 3 — goal to finish (gen 4, #4): the goal's own list, read from where the user wrote it

Task: T-2913 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-4/seed.md row 3 → gen-0.md #4: "Goal to finish. Turn a vague goal into a complete plan: what a finished,
best-in-class version contains, decomposed and ordered. It carries the plan over days, across crashes and
compactions, and knows when it's actually done rather than merely stopped." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted
in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Knowing done from stopped, starting with the goal Sampo is running right now. The live mandate reads "Genesis: build
Foreman into a self-directing harness per research/genesis/gen-0.md §2" and has one item with no check. Read on
2026-11-04: `sampo goal verdict` says "stopped: the goal has no items", and `sampo goal plan` proposes "[model] works
on the web UI surface" four times beside "[standard] it works on the web UI surface", plus proposals naming verbs that don't exist
(`plan`, `stop`). The list the user meant is written down: gen-0 §2's 13 capabilities and its DONE-WHEN line. The plan never
reads the file the goal names. That one line is on the statusline, the SessionStart note, the MCP tool and Smith's

- mandate.py:509 `cmd_plan --apply` gives every added item the one `--done-when` command passed, so a plan can't give

- mandate.py:339: a goal with no items gets the verdict cause "the goal has no items". mandate.py:559

- Callers of the shared read (grep): `mandate.goal_line` at hooks.py:475 (SessionStart), core.py:5612, cli.py:3857,

- gen-0.md:14 holds the DONE-WHEN ("every capability in §2 passes its held-out exam … the completeness sweep (§7) is
  clean, and two generations in a row find no remaining tier 3–4 gap"), and gen-0.md:38-50 the 13 numbered

- The long tier (research/long-false-done.md, T-2556): of 31 failed checks over 12 goals, 9 were "planned but not
  built, or built incomplete": a stated requirement unmet at a done claim. T-2557 checks a goal's own Done-when list.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #4)
- understand × CLI: a goal that names a document is understood as that document's list.
- verify × headless/server: the verdict the night tick and the MCP tool read names unmet items instead of having none.

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
fm mission, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 (research/brainstorm-20261104-002844: 368
distinct ideas; --deepen dropped by today's risk budget, recorded). Grounded:
- "Compile a goal into done-predicates, and compute done from them" and "Map each goal clause to proof, or refuse
  'done'": partial. T-2136's plan and T-2557's Done-when check exist, but a goal that cites a document has no clauses
  to map. Brief 1 supplies them.
- "Turn the six known false dones into a regression corpus": partial. research/long-false-done.md names them, and the
  long tier reruns only at the end of the run (the user's steer). Held for the end-of-run exam.
- "Re-inject a 40-line goal anchor at PreCompact and SessionStart": built near T-2139.
- "Run a worktree and cwd parity matrix over every verb the goal path calls" (lens: the builder in its worktree): new.
  Grounded in friction: `sampo friction` (2026-11-04) shows three `sampo` calls that exited 1 inside a builder
  lane, the first a `sampo lease take`, and seven isolation refusals there. The gen-3 review counted five lease and
  evidence failures ("5× Bash: This agent is isolated in the worktree"). plugin/agents/fm-builder.md:45 tells
  builders to list such refused checks for the main thread. Handed to the next #4 or #9 Mission, since tonight's builds run in those lanes.

## Approaches
1. Cited-document items in `plan`: the named path (repo or project research only, realpath checked), the named
   section, one item per numbered entry and per DONE-WHEN clause; dedupe by text and by grounded target; per-clause
   checks on `--apply`. Likely outcome: the live goal gets 13 capability items plus its DONE-WHEN clauses, and the
   verdict names the open ones. Fails if: a doc's list isn't numbered (top-level bullets then; neither gives no
   items, said out loud).
2. use what exists: `sampo goal item` thirteen times by hand. Fails if: the next goal citing a doc has the same hole.
3. do less: dedupe only. Fails if: the verdict still reads "the goal has no items".
4. Have the model read the file. Fails if: it paraphrases the user's own list, which is drift.

Choice: 1 (70%).

## Exam (an outcome measure, with a live reading)

  verdict "the goal has no items". After: 13 capability items plus the DONE-WHEN clauses, and a verdict that names

- Exam kinds: #4's goal scenarios are unchanged; the long tier reruns at the end of the run (the user's steer).

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
On a replayed long goal whose request points at a spec file, the session's done claim is refused while an entry of
that spec is unmet, and the false-done count of the "planned but not built" class falls.

- Reading untrusted text: the cited file is the repo's own or the project's research. It is read as data, cut to a
  size cap, and never run. A path outside both, or a symlink out, is refused.
- An over-eager item list: a long doc section with dozens of bullets would bury the verdict. Capped (20 items, like

- Callers: none of the eleven call sites changes format. Only the item count grows.

No new verb. One reader in `plan`, a dedupe, a check map. No hook change.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: the run's own goal becomes judgeable.

A live goal whose verdict tracks the 13 capabilities. The next #4 Mission can link each Mission task to its
capability item and let the verdict move as Missions close. The worktree parity idea is carried with its grounding.

# Mission 8 — moonshot (gen 4): regrow Sampo's own code from its intent, and an ecology of minds

Task: T-2918 (brief 1: M-02's slice, plus filing this Mission's ecology moons in the catalogue).

Parent: gen-4/seed.md row 8 → the Moonshot section (far-domain lens: ecology; judged on novelty and value only).
gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Two things this generation, both far from any coverage cell.
1. The floor: advance one extreme or massive moon by a stage. The record points at M-02 (massive, "Keep code as a
   regenerable cache of intent clauses and proofs"). It is the only big moon whose kill test came back viable: 3 of 3
   spec-suite modules were rebuilt blind and passed every original test (bench/moonshot/m02-result.json, T-2679). Its
   kill line names the next stage: "the slice must regenerate a module of Foreman's own, whose spec is its briefs".
   The gen-4 prediction, sealed before the user's next steers, expects the user to ask for exactly this step. The
   standing intent says to act on what the user would say before they say it.
2. The lens: ecology. Moons that borrow a mechanism no harness has and are wild enough that people who build agent
   harnesses ask whether it is even possible (the user's 2026-11-03 steer; never pricing, auction or warranty
   mechanics).

## Grounding (each read on 2026-11-04)
- The catalogue (`sampo moons status`): 58 of 100. Author's tiers: low 1/5, medium 2/10, high 3/15, xhigh 4/20,
  extreme 29/25, massive 19/25. 1 of 18 extreme or massive kill-tested, 0 built. The climb (`sampo moons order`) opens
  with M-18 full (low, unblocks M-02), then kills for M-21 to M-28. Toward the mix means massive and xhigh, not more
  extreme.
- M-02's block: Needs M-18 (prove a rewrite against the old build on recorded inputs), Stage kill. The slice lands
  nothing, so M-18 stays the need of M-02's full build, not of its slice.
- The module set for the slice: in plugin/lib/sampo, 20 leaf modules under 260 lines have their own test file, from
  backtest.py (36 lines, 1 importer) to repeats.py (222 lines, 2 importers). raster.py (156 lines, a 376-line test,
  1 importer) and away.py (102 lines, 141-line test) are typical. Counted by a shell loop over `wc -l` and the test
  files, not chosen by hand.
- The local call and routing: plugin/lib/sampo/models.py:786 `complete`, plugin/lib/sampo/moonscale.py:379 `_local`.
  The 27B's Smith record: `sampo code bench` (state/code-bench.jsonl) closed 1 of 5 seeds on endpoint errors, while
  the 4B and e4b GPU models closed 4 of 5. So the slice names Haiku as its second approach before any not-yet.
- Moons at scale (the user's steer a): `sampo moons coverage` reads 4,879 candidates (3,362 kept, 1,517 rejected),
  420 of 420 grid cells touched, 24 of 24 mechanisms, and the local 27B's keep rate is 83% against Haiku's 36%.
  Mission 6 (T-2916) puts grow and funnel on the nightly timer at $0, which is how the catalogue reaches 10,000.
- Frontier digest: gen-2/frontier.md stands (gen-3/frontier.md: "Off the cadence"). Gen 4 is off the cadence too.
- Not-yet in this campaign: M-12 (no decider beat chance) waits on a close-time forecaster (verification grade and
  unproven kinds). M-13's kill needs 20 answered questions, and the ledger holds 2 `question_answered` rows. Neither is
  unblocked by anything built since. Both carried.

## Ideas (each with its prior art, how ours is better, and a novelty mark)
fm mission, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 with three ecology lenses, inversion, 2030
worked back, bold bets, crossbreeding and an invented lens (research/brainstorm-20261104-003815: 405 distinct ideas;
--deepen dropped by today's risk budget, recorded). Most of its ecology ideas were funnel mechanics (succession-staged
funnels, rarefaction stops, diversity alarms). Those are tools inside a moon, never the moon, so they go to Moonscale's
own backlog. The three below are the wild ones, each crossbred and named with its parents.

### M-59 · Fuse two small models into a lichen that outthinks the frontier model neither can match
- Tier: xhigh
- Domain: model orchestration and small-model uplift
- Lens: ecology: symbiosis (a lichen is an alga and a fungus that become one organism neither can be alone);
  crossbred from "Pair two weak models as a lichen" × "Rate each local model as a symbiont, with a cheater cut-off"
- What: Sampo pairs a fast small model (the alga: a 4B that proposes) with the large local model (the fungus: the 27B
  that holds structure and memory) and evolves the exchange between them over nightly rounds on Sampo's own closed
  tasks: what each passes the other, when, and in what shape. Neither model is fine-tuned. The protocol is the
  organism, kept as a versioned card the pair carries. The jaw-drop is a pair that closes held-out tasks the frontier
  model closes, at no cloud cost, while each partner alone closes half as many.
- Prior art: mixture-of-agents and LLM debate (fixed protocols, peer models); speculative decoding (a small model
  drafts tokens for a large one, by a hand-fixed protocol); Sampo's routing (local first, then Haiku, never a pair).
- Better by: the protocol is evolved and selected on the user's own held-out work, and the pair is judged against the
  frontier arm, not against either partner.
- Novelty: 4
- Needs: T-2878 (a Louhi smith arm on local models), T-2917 (small-model playbooks kept on lift)
- Unblocks: none
- Kill: on 20 train-split Louhi scenarios, run the 4B alone, the 27B alone and three hand-written pair protocols
  (propose and critique, outline and fill, test-first and implement), graded by each scenario's hidden checks.
  Viable if the best pair beats the better partner alone by 5 or more scenarios; not-yet if by 1 or fewer.
- Stage: idea

### M-60 · Grow a mycorrhizal network under every repo on the machine, trading failure shapes as nutrients
- Tier: massive
- Domain: cross-project learning
- Lens: ecology: mycorrhizal networks (fungi join the roots of different trees and carry carbon and alarm signals
  between them); crossbred from "Grow a mycorrhizal lesson network between repos and lanes" × "Federate failure shapes
  between Sampo installs"
- What: Every repo Sampo serves grows hyphae: compressed failure shapes from its proven fixes, the outline of a bug's
  syntax and data flow and never its code. The network carries each shape to repos whose code is near it, and a repo
  that receives one is warned before it writes that bug. Trees that fix more feed more. A sensitive repo neither sends
  nor receives. Over months the network learns which of the user's repos are kin, and a new repo is inoculated from
  its nearest kin on day one.
- Prior art: GitHub's multi-repository variant analysis (people write the query for one known bug); Semgrep registry
  rules (shared by hand); federated learning (shares gradients, not failure shapes); Sampo's lessons (one project's).
- Better by: shapes move by measured kinship between the user's own repos, unasked, and a delivered warning counts
  only when the receiving repo later fixes that shape.
- Novelty: 4
- Needs: a failure-shape miner from proven FIX tasks (the miner M-22 also needs), kinship from import graphs and stack
  cards, a cross-project store under the sensitive rule
- Unblocks: M-22
- Kill: over every project in Sampo's state with 5 or more proven FIX tasks, ask of each fix whether a shape mined
  from another project's earlier fixes flags the lines the fix changed, before the fix, at under one false flag per
  2,000 lines. Report each project's era (first and last fix date) and fail the run if the eras don't overlap.
  Viable if 10% or more of fixes were foreseen by a kin repo; not-yet if under 3%.
- Stage: idea

### M-61 · Breed a Red Queen: a predator that evolves new bugs against Sampo's own detectors every night
- Tier: massive
- Domain: verification by adversarial co-evolution
- Lens: ecology: Red Queen dynamics (predator and prey must keep evolving to stay where they are); crossbred from "Run
  a Red Queen arms race between generator and critic" × "Reintroduce an apex predator into the funnel"
- What: A predator lineage on the local models writes plausible bugs into throwaway copies of the user's repos, aimed
  at slipping past Sampo's finders, guard, review lenses and tests. Every bug that escapes is a lesson the prey (the
  detectors) must learn before the next night, and every detector that improves forces the predator to evolve. Both
  populations are scored, and the arms race's trace is a living map of where Sampo is blind.
- Prior art: mutation testing (random, not adaptive); coverage-guided fuzzing (finds crashes, not quiet logic bugs);
  GANs (images, not code); LLM red-teaming (prompts); Sampo's hunk-mutation proof (T-0271), which mutates one task's
  hunks once.
- Better by: the bug writer adapts to the detectors Sampo actually runs, and the detectors are scored only on bugs
  nobody wrote for them, on the user's own code.
- Novelty: 4
- Needs: T-2910 (local brainstorm volume), the exam's planted-defect renderer, a night slot (T-2916)
- Unblocks: M-22
- Kill: on the exam's throwaway repos, have the local 27B write 100 bugs over three rounds, each round shown which
  earlier bugs `sampo find` caught. Viable if the third round's escape rate is at least twice the first's (the
  predator learns); not-yet if it is flat.
- Stage: idea

The novelty marks above are the author's. `fm genesis novelty` marks the obvious ones by a cold read, and a typed mark
counts for nothing.

## The spike: M-02's slice (brief 1)
`sampo regen PATH --model PROFILE` works in a throwaway worktree only. It removes the module and gives a tool-less
model the module's intent and never its code: the Raw request, Interpretation and criteria of every brief whose
scope or touched files name it, its MASTER.md entry, its test file and the names its importers use. The reply is
checked (it compiles, and imports nothing the original didn't), written, and the module's own tests run, each result
printed. There are two tries, and the main checkout is never written. The slice run covers all 20 leaf modules, with
the 27B first and Haiku second where the 27B fails, its sample stated before it runs and its result kept beside the
script (T-2721, T-2724).

## Approaches
1. `sampo regen` as a verb plus the slice run over the leaf set. Likely outcome: a round-trip rate per module, and
   the failures show where Sampo's briefs and tests don't pin its code, which is M-02's claim. Fails if: briefs
   written as change requests are too thin to rebuild anything. Then not-yet with that blocker and both approaches.
2. use what exists: rerun kill_m02.py on Sampo modules. Fails if: it is a script, not the working slice the stage
   asks for.
3. do less: one module by hand. Fails if: it is one anecdote, and nothing reruns it.
4. Regenerate and land on green tests. Fails if: passing tests isn't equivalence on real inputs. That is M-18, the
   full build's need.

Choice: 1 on the leaf set (60%). The doubt is real, and a failure is a finding.

## Exam
No exam kind (a moonshot is judged on novelty and value). The slice's check: of the 20 leaf modules, 2 or more
round-trip (every original test green) on the 27B or, second, on Haiku → "Advanced: M-02 slice (T-2918)" goes into
this file and the catalogue's Stage line becomes slice, with Evidence: T-2918. Fewer → not-yet.md gets M-02's slice
with its blocker and both approaches, and M-02 stays at kill. Measure (for the catalogue's Measure: line): the
round-trip rate over the leaf set, rerun each generation, where a rising rate means intent and proofs pin more code.

## Campaign (MOONSHOT.md part A)
- Planned: M-02 slice (T-2918). The Advanced line is written only when the slice result is filed.
- Added toward the mix: M-59 (xhigh), M-60 (massive), M-61 (massive), each with a Kill line. T-2918 files them in
  moonshot.md and runs `sampo moons rate`, so the strongest model tiers them blind.
- Carried: M-12 and M-13 not-yet (see Grounding). M-18 full stays first in the climb as M-02's full-build need.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
Any module of Sampo's can be deleted and regrown from its intent and proofs on a local model, and the modules that
can't are the ones whose briefs and tests are listed as too weak, each with a task to strengthen them.

## Risks
- Leakage: the module's code must never reach the prompt. Its docstring, comments and any MASTER.md line that quotes
  code are cut. A test holds that no line of the original appears in the prompt.
- Running model code: a reply runs only inside the throwaway worktree, under the module's own tests, after a compile
  and import check. Nothing lands.
- Overlap with Mission 5: T-2915 moves MASTER.md's module entries into docs/map shards. `regen` reads the entry
  through the same union helper, or whichever lands second adapts.
- Spend: the 27B first, at $0. Haiku only where it fails, inside the per-command cap.

## Lean
One verb that later becomes M-02's standing check. The slice script is a run of that verb, not a second code path.
No hook.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 4: no harness regrows its own modules from intent as a check on how well that intent pins them.

## Hands to the next generation
The round-trip table per module. M-02's full build waits on M-18. The three ecology moons wait on their kill tests:
M-60 and M-61 are massive and get the cheapest kill next generation, and M-59's kill waits on T-2878's smith arm.

## Done when
T-2918's four criteria are green, the slice result and the M-02 stage (or its not-yet entry) are filed, the three
moons are in the catalogue and `sampo moons check` passes, and MASTER.md and CHANGELOG say it.

# Mission 6 — self-triggering (gen 4, #11): the night shift runs on the local models

Task: T-2916 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-4/seed.md row 6 → gen-0.md #11: "Self-triggering. Schedules, file and event triggers, CI and issue
watchers, so work starts without me. Installs (timers, units) get queued for one yes." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs
are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Work that starts by itself and costs nothing. The schedule is there: `systemctl --user list-timers` (2026-11-04)
shows foreman-night-foreman-4a056f firing nightly at 02:30 and foreman-tick-foreman-4a056f hourly. Both were
installed through the one-yes queue. What the night does is the gap. `sampo night --dry-run` plans 10 jobs tonight,
about $1.80 of a $2.00 limit: eight free chores with no model (scout, dream, cold files, guard cases, steer checks,
compost, consolidate, sentinel) and two paid calls (landscape, queue). It skips the court for money. The local models
sit idle all night, though the user asked for them to be used "without limit" for volume (standing steers a and b).
The work they are best at is already built and routes local first: Moons grow and the Moons funnel. The catalogue
stands at 4,879 candidates against the 10,000 target (`sampo moons coverage`), and it grows only when a session runs
it by hand.

## Grounding (each read in the code on 2026-11-04)
- plugin/lib/sampo/night.py:51 `jobs(p)` lists tonight's (name, argv, USD) jobs. No job calls a local model; the only
  model work is paid (`second session`, `landscape`, `model lesion`, `pre-plan`, `research debt`, `court`, `evolve
  candidate`, `queue`, `draft`).
- night.py:553-585: `cmd_night` (night.py:483) fits jobs under the limit, then runs them one at a time as `fm`
  subprocesses with the breaker (`serve.FAILS_MAX`, night.py:575), the usage check (night.py:569), the panic check and
  a heartbeat. Each job gets `JOB_TIMEOUT` (night.py:25, 3 hours). A $0 job always fits.
- plugin/lib/sampo/moonscale.py:428 `grow` runs `workers` calls at once (default: the local profile's slots) and stops
  at its target, its call cap, the budget or a run of failures. moonscale.py:834 `funnel` runs the exact, embed, kill,
  tier and novelty stages. All of them ask through moonscale.py:397 `_ask`, which tries the local profile first and
  falls back to Haiku with no way to refuse the fallback. That fallback is what a night must not take silently.
- moonscale.py:379 `_local`: own or loopback profiles only, loopback only for a sensitive project. Night already
  refuses to run anything in a sensitive project ("sensitive project: nothing runs at night").
- `sampo moons coverage` (2026-11-04): "Kept by model: haiku 545 of 1499, jarvis+nothink 2753 of 3316, jarvis+think
  64 of 64". The local model's candidates survive the write-time rules far more often than Haiku's, so local-only
  costs no quality here.
- The trigger table (`sampo triggers`): the `night` trigger has fired once. The schedule exists, and almost nothing
  rides it.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #11)
- operate × headless/server: a nightly job that uses the machine's own models with no session and no spend.
- build × headless/server: the Moons catalogue grows toward its target without a person starting it.

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
fm mission, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 (research/brainstorm-20261104-003735: 349
distinct ideas; --deepen dropped by today's risk budget, recorded). Grounded:
- "Route background volume to the local model first" (round 1): new for the night run, built for Moons. Brief 1 joins
  them.
- "Stop the night on spend and disk, not only on usage limits": built near T-1476. The night stops at its spend limit
  and on usage (night.py:563-571). Disk is not a stop condition. Held.
- "Wild: Yield the GPU the moment the user shows up" and "Start and stop the night on logind lock and unlock": new.
  The night runs at 02:30, so a user at the machine is rare. Held for the next #11 Mission, with "Mark every
  local-made result unwitnessed until verified" (the funnel's verdicts already carry their model).
- "Write a sealed night plan and a morning card graded against it" (round 4) and the cross-bred "Supervise the night
  from outside with typed stops and catch-up": partial. The night ledger event records ran, skipped and stopped. A
  graded morning card is the next step once the night does real work.

## Approaches
1. Two $0 jobs, `moons grow` and `moons funnel` with call caps and `--local-only`, listed only while a local model
   answers and the store is under target. Likely outcome: about two thousand candidates a night, funnelled, at $0.
   Fails if: the local server drops mid-run; local-only stops the job with its reason, still at $0.
2. use what exists: run `moons grow` by hand. Fails if: it needs a session, which #11 exists to remove.
3. do less: the grow job only. Fails if: unfunnelled rows pile up as filler.
4. A separate local-model timer. Fails if: it is a new install waiting on a yes, and it duplicates the night's
   safeties.

Choice: 1 (75%).

## Exam (an outcome measure, with a live reading)
- Outcome measure: the catalogue's size and funnel counts in the morning, read from `sampo moons coverage`, against
  4,879 candidates and 3,362 kept today. It is read after a night has run (the window rule), and paid spend on the
  `moons` and `moons-funnel` features that night is $0 (`sampo cost`).
- Live reading at close: `sampo night --dry-run` lists both jobs at $0.00 with the local model up, and a run with the
  model stopped lists neither.
- Exam kinds: #11's trigger scenarios are unchanged. A machine's state (a model up or down) is a unit test, not an
  exam variant (the self-triggering critique's rule).

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
The user wakes to measured work the machine did on its own models: more candidates, funnelled, with the night's
ledger saying what ran and why it stopped.

## Risks
- Spend leak through the fallback: the reason for `--local-only`. A test plants a dead local profile and asserts no
  Haiku call.
- GPU contention with the bench or Smith: night jobs run one at a time, each with a call cap.
- Catalogue quality: the funnel job runs after grow in the same night, and the write-time rules still reject
  internal-only and untestable rows.
- Privacy: a sensitive project runs nothing at night (existing), and local means own or loopback only.

## Lean
No new verb, no new unit, no hook. Two job rows and one flag.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3: self-triggered work on the machine's own models, the user's standing ask.

## Hands to the next generation
The night's growth per run and its stop reasons. Next on the same rail: T-2910's local brainstorm as a night job for
the next Mission's ideas, the model bench rerun nightly (T-2886), and the graded morning card.

## Done when
T-2916's three criteria are green, one real night has run both jobs (its ledger event read in the critique), and
MASTER.md (fmnight, Moonscale) and CHANGELOG say it.

# Mission 4 — verifying anything (gen 4, #6): meaning checked when the plan is written

Task: T-2914 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-4/seed.md row 4 → gen-0.md #6: "Verifying anything. Proof beyond unit tests: UI (`fm shot`, `fm flow`),
data, docs against code, infra and ops, performance, and "does it do what the user meant". Whatever can't be proven
gets labelled as unproven." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
"Does it do what the user meant", proven per clause, at the moment proof is cheapest. Meaning is the largest unproven
class: `sampo prove --rollup` (2026-11-04) counts 767 unproven over 30 days, 599 of them meaning. The gen-3 critique
named it as #6's next lever: "fm spec's example assertions become runnable criteria at plan time, with no
confirmation step; a meaning label clears only when such a criterion ran green." Before naming a fix, this Mission
counted what each candidate would clear (the staying-lean critique's rule):
- Every shown reason is "no criterion checks it" (900 of the 900 reasons the rollup prints; it cuts each task to 3).
  None is "no green run" or "couldn't fail". The clauses are missing checks, not failing ones.
- By whose words: of the 599, 113 are user-sourced briefs. 273 are Sampo's own (discovered 159, followup 55, self 20,
  baseline 14, ci 12, genesis 7, genesis-review 3, steer 2, scout 1). 213 are archived briefs the index doesn't carry.
  The most common unproven clauses are Sampo's provenance notes, not requests: "(noticed by an agent;" 52, "Plugin
  parity: usable from Claude Code" 16, "Captured by fm check: the gates are red" 15, "Baseline red" 11.
- So the count mixes two things. The user's words lack criteria at plan time: 53 of 302 user M and L closes in the
  rollup's window carry the label. Sampo's notes were never anyone's meaning.
The brief does both halves honestly. The plan gate asks for the missing check while it is cheap. The rollup prints
the two counts side by side, adding up to today's 599, and drops nothing. That is the gen-3 review's lesson: the docs
kind's 601 → 421 "fell by narrowing what counts, not by proving anything".

## Grounding (each read in the code on 2026-11-04)
- plugin/lib/sampo/recall.py:691 `bind(b)` binds each Raw-request clause (CONTEXT lines aside) to the criterion
  sharing 2+ words. recall.py:718 `meaning_unproven` keeps those with no green, failable check.
- plugin/lib/sampo/core.py:4928 `_need_meaning` turns them into the label, and core.py:4937 registers
  `PROOF_KINDS["meaning"]`. It is a label, never a block.
- core.py:3130 `plan_gaps` is the plan gate (`sampo focus` refuses until it is empty). It calls `_content_gaps`
  (core.py:3019) for briefs not yet started, skips harness plans (`harness_plan`) and requires criteria. It never
  calls `bind`, so a plan can pass with a whole clause unchecked.
- Callers of the shared read (grep): `_content_gaps` is also called by Smith's M-plan check at smith.py:286 on a stub
  brief, which carries no source. The new gap lives in `plan_gaps`, not `_content_gaps`, so Smith's check is
  unchanged. `meaning_unproven` has one caller (core.py:4931).
- plugin/lib/sampo/change.py:65 `cmd_spec` writes assertions, but only for a Python `--module`, so it can't be the
  plan-time route for most clauses (UI, docs, process). It stays the route for a Python wish.
- Steer (d), the user's 2026-11-03 ask that public surfaces name models by role and the orchestrator as any agent: it
  is built and tested (T-2852: site/build.py:574-579 and site/genesis/genesis.js:86-89 rewrite the local endpoint's
  name to "a large local model"; test_genesis.py and test_site_sections.py hold it). Read here, not rebuilt.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #6)
- plan × Claude Code: the plan gate a Claude Code session meets asks for each clause's check before the first edit.
- verify × CLI: the rollup's meaning count says whose words are unproven.

## Ideas (from the brainstorm, grounded)
fm mission, then fm ideas --rounds 4 --falsify --crossbreed --seen-latest 6 (research/brainstorm-20261104-002904: 329
distinct ideas; --deepen dropped by today's risk budget, recorded). Grounded:
- "Turn spec examples into runnable criteria at plan time" (round 1): partial. `sampo spec` makes assertions for a

  verdict, and show proved against unproven everywhere": partial. The rollup is two-valued per kind. The split by

- "Gate shipping on a role-word vocabulary lint driven by one role table" (cross-bred, steer d): built near T-2852
  (the render-time rewrite and its tests). Not rebuilt.

## Approaches
1. A plan-time gap from `recall.bind` in `plan_gaps` for user M and L briefs, plus a rollup split by whose words.
   Likely outcome: new user M and L closes stop arriving with meaning unproven. Fails if: bind's two-word rule binds a

2. use what exists: `sampo spec` per wish. Fails if: Python-only, `--module` required.
3. do less: split the count only. Fails if: no clause gets proven, and the user count keeps growing.
4. A local model drafts each missing criterion. Fails if: drafted checks are written to pass. Held for T-2878.

Choice: 1 (70%).

## Exam (an outcome measure, with a live reading)
- Outcome measure: the share of user M and L closes that land with meaning unproven, from the rollup, for closes after
  T-2914 against 53 of 302 before. It counts once those closes exist. A close inside its window is read when the

- Exam kinds: #6's proof scenarios are unchanged; the end-of-run exam reads them.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
Every clause a user writes in an M or L request has a failable check before its first edit, and the rollup's
user's-words count falls by proof, not by relabelling.

## Risks

The user's, under gen-0 and over every later steer (T-2191; every cold read sees it too):

A harness that figures out and does everything itself. The user's only jobs are gen-0's goals and a yes to what leaves the machine or touches protected core. Every steer is a miss to learn from.

1. Anticipate: generalize the pattern behind each steer; before filing a tower doc, ask what the user would say if they read it now, and act on that first; more ambitious, complete, general and honest, with less hand-holding.
